Title: Approaching the euro
Subtitle: Speech by Mr Marian Jusko, Governor of the National Bank of Slovakia, at the Conference "Challenges of EU Accession", Prague, 1 April 2003.
text: Marian Jusko: Approaching the euro Speech by Mr Marian Jusko, Governor of the National Bank of Slovakia, at the Conference "Challenges of EU Accession", Prague, 1 April 2003. * * * Ladies and Gentlemen, I welcome the opportunity to address you tonight and I would like to thank the CNB for including me into this panel, where I can speak and discuss the most challenging and demanding topic, which is the EMU accession. We all, central bankers, know that the main role will not be played by us, but crucial will be the decision and actual steps of national governments. Let me present the views and approach of the National Bank of Slovakia, which, however, cannot be considered as the official statement of the Slovak Republic. Nowadays, there is the joint strategy of the central bank and the government under preparation, which will be approved by the Slovak Government in the second quarter and which will also be a part of our PEP (pre-accession economic programme). The intention here is to officially announce the term of our preparedness for examination, which also serves as the yardstick and anchor for all our current and future decisions. The general approach of the NBS, which can be slightly (in terms of its schedule) modified by our government, is the earliest possible approach towards the euro adoption and EMU membership. At the same time, we prefer the shortest possible membership in the ERM II mechanism. The main idea behind the formulation of the earliest possible strategy of EMU accession is our belief that Slovakia may enter the EMU earlier, but must not become a member of the eurozone later than other associated countries. This is based on our latest experience, when we were treated as an outsider in the second wave of the EU, OECD and NATO enlargement, with a long lasting effect on FDI inflows, costs of debt service and the overall macroeconomic development. I do not want to bother you with all these well-known and clear reasons for entering the EMU, which are, above all, the savings on transaction costs and a decline in the exchange rate volatility and exchange rate risk. This is extremely important for Slovakia with its high level of openness. The share of exports and imports of goods and services in GDP increased to 156.5% in 2001 from 117.3% in 1993, while 60% of exports and 50% of imports were related to EU countries in 2001. After including the CEC5, these shares would increase to 89% for exports and 71% for imports. Considering the large share of the Slovak foreign trade in GDP and the territorial structure of the foreign trade, the probable positive impact of the increased openness due to the EMU membership (an estimated increase of 1.6 percentage points) on the GDP per capita growth may oscillate around 1%. We are also aware of disadvantages which could be connected with the EMU membership. Among frequently mentioned disadvantages of the euro adoption belong the ongoing process of catching up with EU levels, the insufficiently synchronised business cycles and the loss of the exchange rate stabiliser. Along with this, we get the common monetary policy which is doubtful to fit to all, especially to a country with structural changes still ahead. With regard to the above mentioned possibly problematic areas, in our view, the real and nominal convergence can be seen as complementary to each other, and should be pursued in parallel. Over the short period of time, a contradiction between the real and nominal convergence has become evident where GDP growth could slow down. However, at the same time, conditions for more dynamic and, mainly, sustainable growth will be created. Under these conditions Slovakia has a potential for the GDP grow of around 4-5% in the medium term. Regarding the independent monetary policy and the automatic stabiliser of the exchange rate, let me ask the question: Is it possible, in such a small and open country, that they would work freely and independently? I can openly say that we do not see any serious problem in meeting all Maastricht criteria in the medium-term horizon. However, what could negatively effect fulfilment of fiscal criteria and slightly postpone the process of integration is the treatment of the pension reform expenditures, which is now also in question in many associated as well as member countries. 19/2003 1 In the end, let me stress that there is a strong incentive and first steps have already been carried out in the area of structural reforms, particularly those related to the pension, health-care and social benefits policies, and decentralisation. The price distortions are expected to narrow in 2004. The plan of the Ministry of Finance is to lower the fiscal deficit from around 6% in 2002 to 5% in 2003 and to 3,4% in 2004, so that Slovakia could be ready for the examination in 2005 or 2006. Thank you for your attention. 2 19/2003

Title: Slovakia - perspective place for investments
Subtitle: Speech by Ms Elena Kohutikova, Deputy Governor of the National Bank of Slovakia, at the Conference Middle and East Europe ...
text: Elena Kohutikova: Slovakia - perspective place for investments Speech by Ms Elena Kohutikova, Deputy Governor of the National Bank of Slovakia, at the Conference Middle and East Europe  region of the future, Salzburg, 15 October 2003. * * * Slovakia has been disregarded as a reasonable country to place an investment in, for a long time. This trend has been showing on the results of total foreign direct investments made in Slovakia until 1999 compared to the other countries acceding to the European Union in May 2004. After the changes of general economic policy (economic reforms, legislative changes, making institutions more transparent) with the new government seizing power in 1998, this FDI per capita gap shrinked to minimum. At present, overall environment is very much competitive for new investments within the area; it still ranks fourth behind Czech rep., Hungary and Poland, however capacity to invest, experience of the foreign companies that invested already and overall conditions created by government motivation to attract new investments makes Slovakia a very interesting market. This contribution aims to view some of the attributes of Slovak environment and features of the country that have a vast importance in the course of decision-making process on placement of an investment. 1. Location and infrastructure Slovakia is a small open economy (with exports plus imports ratio to GDP amounting to 155 %). Therefore, development of external relations is of high importance for the country. Thanks to location, Slovakia, near European markets as well as near eastern European emerging markets may represent a bridge between East and West. European market of 350 million people is accessible within one-day truck drive (more than U.S. and Canada combined). Despite relatively hilly surface, major roads infrastructure is fairly well developed. Moreover, government highway construction program aims to conclude main corridors connecting North and South, and East and West in the medium resp. long run perspective. 2. External stability Slovakia became a member of OECD in 2000. This membership invitation declared stable environment, transparency and clear path in economic development based on the premises of the World Trade Organization. OECD membership itself helped to certain extent to ensure exponential growth of investments in 2000-2002. Slovakia will enter European Union in May 2004 and soon will become a member of NATO as well (ratification process in member countries is running in the moment). Economy has been stabilized and Maastricht criteria should be reached and fulfilled until 2006. According to the strategy, Slovakia plans to adopt euro as soon as possible, on the horizon of years 2008-2010. 3. Internal stability A) Reforms All necessary economic reforms were/are to be introduced before fulfilling Maastricht criteria that the least possible disturbing factors may appear once given up own monetary tools. Pension reform is under the process of final discussion in the Parliament, new Labor Act has been introduced recently, major tax reform is to be introduced soon and health care reform and public administration reform is underway as well. Another major reform, tax reform, aims to make the tax system more transparent and simple. This unique and radical reform based on fiscal neutrality introduces unified flat tax rate of 19% for VAT and rise of other indirect taxes on the one hand and introduces the same, decreased, direct tax rate of 19% for individual income tax as well as corporate tax on the other hand. This reform will change the situation of both companies and households dramatically. It also counts with gradual delegation of minor taxes and fees to the lower level, to communities, which will collect these to relocate resources for projects developing local infrastructure and solution of the ecology related problems. 46/2003 1 Pension reform introduces three-pillar system. The first pay-as-you-go pillar fulfils the role of full merit and the second capitalization pillar fulfills the role of pension savings; both of which will be obligatory. The third supplementary pillar fulfills the role of additional pension insurance choice. The objective of this reform is to adjust the system to demographic changes and to changing features of the society. This reform is assumed to bring more effective management of the social system in future. Healthcare reform aims to solve two main issues. These are introduction of deductibles for health care services. Two functions of this measure shall prevent misuse of free healthcare services and collect resources in order to support financial stability of the system. Moreover, the reform includes other stabilization measures, which aim to slow down or even stop the sector indebtedness. Public finances reform aims to make public finances more transparent as well, introduces strategic planned budgeting and more effective allocation of resources. This reform includes introduction of forecasting systems for stable medium-term framework of public finances. All these and other introduced and planned reforms are structured in detail, timed and co-organized with all other important economic interventions as well as with ability to comply with Maastricht criteria, especially budget deficit. 3. Internal Stability B) Fiscal and monetary consolidation In 2002, the general government deficit amounted to 7.2% of GDP, which was well above the reference value set for EMU admission. Slovakia had also failed to meet this particular criterion in the previous years. The largest deficit had been recorded in 2000, surging largely on the back of costs incurred in restructuring the banking sector, with after-effects of the restructuring campaign still affecting the deficit through interest expenses. Based on the draft assumptions of the state budget of following years, the Slovak government is bent on slashing the deficit down to 5.0% of GDP in 2003 and 3.9% of GDP in 2004, In 2005, the deficit is supposed to reach 3.4 percent. In 2006, the criterion regarding the general government deficit should be met with a small margin to spare (0.1%). The fiscal criterion on public debt is currently met. Slovakia had not exceeded the reference value (60% of GDP) in the previous years either. After a gradual increase in public debt in the period of 1999-2001, in 2002 the government moved to reduce it, in particular by using privatisation revenues. The inflation was above the reference value throughout the entire period reviewed, but shows a downtrend in the last years. At the end of 2002, Slovakia's HICP exceeded the reference value of 2.9% by a mere 0.4%. However, massive price deregulations implemented in 2003 leaded to a substantial increase in inflation, which currently exceeds 8%. Deregulation effects will be present also in 2004, but their share should slowly decrease and in 2006 total inflation will not exceed 3%. This will lead to fulfillment of inflation criterion for our eurozone entry. Considering the fact that there is only a limited amount of bond issues in Slovakia with long term maturity, it is useful to look at the development on the yield till maturity on the traded long term bonds. These have been falling in the recent years, with the yield till maturity below 5 per cent to meet the Maastricht criteria. The SKK/EUR exchange rate was relatively stable during the period reviewed, namely from early 2001 until now. It spent most of the time in a 3% corridor off the mean value of SKK/EUR 42.63 (average for the period from 1 January 2001 until now). It recorded a period low in July 2002 amid pre-election doubts, and is currently (September 2003) attacking its highs as the Slovak currency is considered the most stable and attractive in the Central European region. 4. Dynamics of the growth Based on a comparison of real GDP growth in Slovakia and in the EU, we can find a more distinct convergence of economic levels in the last two years. In 2002, real GDP growth in Slovakia outpaced real GDP growth in the EU by more than 3 percentage points. In GDP growth, Slovakia is one of the most dynamic economies and this should persist also in the following years. 2 46/2003 In 2002, Slovakia has absorbed the highest inflow of foreign direct investments in its entire history; the total inflow amounted to 185.8 billion SKK, i.e. almost 4.5 billion EUR. In other words the inflow of foreign direct investments was two times higher than in 2000 and more than 20 times higher than in 1997. Following results of a recent survey done by Forbes magazine, 91% of current foreign investors in Slovakia intend to increase their stakes. The group of present and satisfied investors is getting bigger, the group covers names like: Alcatel, Coca-Cola, Fujitsu, Heineken, IBM, Johnson Controls, Kraft, MOL, Samsung, Siemens, Sony, Tesco, US Steel, VW, etc.. Taking into account current and future VW investments and lately confirmed PSA Peugeot-Citroen investment plans, Slovakia is on its way to become one of the leading automobile producers. Industrial production absorbed more than 36 % of total foreign direct investments and another significant amount (24.5%) came into financial intermediation. 5. Labour force A steadily growing economy, solid growth in labor productivity and the expansion of investor activity in Slovakia are positive signals both for the economic development as well as for investment climate for new players to arrive. Besides, Slovakia possesses relatively high quality of education system and the skills of its labor force. Businesses operating in Slovakia have discovered that the work force has in general strong work ethic, is skilled and educated. Slovakias school system ensures that almost 90% of the population has secondary or university education. With wages lower than Hungary, Poland or the Czech Republic, employee costs even lower that in European Union; Slovakia becomes even more attractive for investments. As candidate countries try to catch up with the EU, it is critical that GDP growths to be supported by rising productivity of labour, while factors of costs are kept under control. During last 10 years Slovakia achieved 4% growth in the real productivity of labour and 2% growth in the real wage. Past development in the real unit labour costs is even more favourable for foreign investments. Slovakia offers the lowest labour and production costs among V4 countries. This low labor and production costs have roots mainly in the character of labor market and features of unemployment, which is still, in spite of down-sloping trend, one of the highest in the region. However, availability of this workforce, which is relatively skilled, represents another advantage. Industrial restructuring and transformation have led to a high level of redundancy of skilled labor force. Stateowned heavy industry and weaponry, running before 1990, were liquidated or went bankrupt. After the period of low foreign investments until 1999, job creation dropped into red numbers. This trend has been reverted after 2000; however still large numbers of industry oriented skilled workers mainly in central and eastern parts of the country are searching for job opportunities. 6. Legislative investment incentives The trend of introducing legislation that favors foreign direct investments has been gradually approved since 1999. The Parliament had approved several major acts; the main goal of is to stimulate foreign direct investments to Slovak economy. The main acts, as follows, create the baseline to the motivation of foreign direct investments be placed in Slovakia. The Investment Incentive Act no. 565/2001 deals with state support in forms of:  initial investments to tangible and intangible assets  subsidies for newly created job opportunities (up to USD 4.000)  subsidies for re-qualification of employees hired to newly created job opportunities (up to 230 USD) Industrial Park Development Support Act no. 193/2001 is another important basic investment incentive, which deals with community subsidies for:  technical facilities and infrastructure up to 70% of total costs  land purchase costs up to 70% of total costs 46/2003 3  land rental costs up to 70% within next 10 years to the community ownership or community disposal to the use of the developer. All customs and import duties on new machinery employed in production have been canceled, well before the adoption of free movement of good, when this issue will become automatic. All these and other allowances even more support all the points that make an investment in Slovakia even more attractive. 7. Rating improvement All the features discussed and measures taken in the scope of Slovak economic development mirror in the continuous improvement of rating by all major rating agencies. Conclusion Slovakia has taken many steps in order to become more attractive place to make an investment, mainly in the recent years. Moreover, it is obvious that economy is on the path to stabilization, both external and internal. All major reforms are timed in the way to be introduced before 2005 and more importantly before joining ERM2. Legislation favoring foreign investments has been applied to a large extent. Labor and production costs are one of the lowest in the region. Vast majority of investors are satisfied and confident about future. Besides, Slovakia experiences one of the highest dynamics in the region. All these features make Slovakia a more perspective country to invest day by day. 4 46/2003

Title: Euro implementation in Slovakia
Subtitle: Speech by Mr Ivan Sramko, Governor of the National Bank of Slovakia, at the Opening of the European Central Bank Exhibition in the National Bank of Slovakia, Bratislava, 24 September 2008.
text: Ivan Sramko: Euro implementation in Slovakia Speech by Mr Ivan Sramko, Governor of the National Bank of Slovakia, at the Opening of the European Central Bank Exhibition in the National Bank of Slovakia, Bratislava, 24 September 2008. * * * I am pleased to welcome you at the present ceremonial opening of the Exhibition of the European Central Bank about euro and on the eve of a big international conference on euro implementation in Slovakia. It is more than symbolic that this exhibition is located just here, on the grounds of the National Bank of Slovakia. Already from the very beginning, when the initiatives for euro implementation in our country were only emerging, the NBS several times declared its support for the entry into the monetary union as soon as practicable. Our recommendations were based on serious analysis  we were assessing the readiness of our economy for the EU membership, we were evaluating how quickly the Slovak economy would be able to approach the economies of the countries within Eurozone, we were assessing the possibilities to comply with the Maastricht criteria from the points of time and costs. Of course, we were considering both favourable and unfavourable impacts of our future membership in Eurozone. According to all the analysis available the benefits were clearly prevailing. The development of euro implementation strategy in 2003 and later on the creation of the National Plan of Euro Implementation in 2005 followed. The predictions and analysis were the basis for setting the economic policy that ensured smooth preparation of our economy to euro. At present, all the decisions and assessments are known and with the New Year the common currency will become a part of our everyday life. By accepting the euro as the national currency Slovakia will become the member of a strong club of Monetary Union states and a new space will be opened for our country for its stabile economic development which will be reflected in other aspects of our lives. Hundreds of people from various institutions have been participating at various projects relating to the access of euro. Many of them have been the employees of the National Bank of Slovakia. I would like to thank all of them for their efforts and persistency by which they significantly contributed to the fact than on January 1, 2009, Slovakia will become the 16th country of Eurozone. I would also like to thank the colleagues from the ECB and partner central banks for their support and co-operation. Ladies and gentlemen, I believe we will all get used to euro in the course of time and that euro will become a natural part of our lives. I wish you manage the euro transition smoothly and without any problems and that euro brings a positive change into in your lives. 117/2008 1

Title: Opening remarks - Tenth anniversary of the euro in Slovakia
Subtitle: Opening remarks by Mr Jozef Makuch, Governor of the National Bank of Slovakia, at the International Conference to mark the tenth anniversary of the introduction of the euro in Slovakia, Bratislava, 11 January 2019.
text: _____________________________________________________________ Narodna banka Slovenska Communication Section OPENING REMARKS by Mr Jozef Makuch, Governor of Narodna banka Slovenska at the conference 10 YEARS OF THE URO IN SLOVAKIA International Conference to Mark the 10th Anniversary of the Introduction of the Euro in Slovakia Bratislava, 11 January 2019 Dear Deputy Prime Minister Kazimir, Dear Mr Mersch, our honoured guest from the ECB Executive Board, Dear Governors, Ladies and gentlemen, It is my great pleasure to welcome so many distinguished guests to this conference, organised to mark the 10th anniversary of euro adoption in Slovakia. Ten years ago, when we were just switching to the euro, or even 15 years ago, when we started preparing for euro accession, we believed this would be the pinnacle of our integration process. We were coming from a small emerging market economy with volatile capital flows and unexpected foreign exchange pressures. We were looking forward to becoming part of the worlds largest economy and the second most important global currency. It turns out we have got both more and less than we expected. On the one hand, we got not only a monetary union, but also a banking union, soon a capital markets union, and to some degree also a fiscal union. Ten years after our euro area entry, and ten years after the outbreak of the global financial crisis, the European monetary union is more complete than ever but still needs a lot of work. I am sure many of our distinguished speakers will be discussing what needs to be done to bring it to completion. Narodna banka Slovenska, Imricha Karvasa 1, 813 25 Bratislava, Slovak Republic On the other hand, we also got less from the changeover than we hoped. No matter how happy the wedding, there will always be rough patches in the marriage: every union requires constant efforts from the partners to function well. The debt crisis in some euro area countries has shown us that the euro is still vulnerable to shocks. From a domestic perspective, not all the expected benefits of the euro have fully materialised. One reason is that the crisis slowed our convergence towards the most developed economies. Another reason is that the global slowdown in trade weighed on the most important channels of monetary union benefits. A third reason is that our domestic policies have not always been optimal: the reform momentum stalled and long-term growth was not always a priority. Certainly some of our panellists will be exploring these aspects further. At this point, I would like to recall Slovakias successful preparations for the euro. While the euro was, and still is, a political project  both in the EU and in Slovakia  it is also based on sound economic fundamentals. From a political economy point of view, our euro adoption process was a role model of economic policymaking. We analysed the costs and benefits very deeply  and given the information set we had at the time, most of the analyses are still valid. All the analyses were openly published. We discussed the project with all relevant stakeholders and tried to make sure no one was left behind. We set a target date for euro adoption and ended up being one of the very few countries that never shifted the target adoption date. And today, ten years on, we are looking back with an open mind to see which of the expectations were fulfilled and which were not. As you well know, the final decision on our euro accession was made in July 2008, just before the global financial crisis broke out in September. We could not have hoped for better timing. The euro shielded us from the initial hit of the crisis, while in other emerging markets, exchange rates plummeted. The drop in demand and in oil and food prices at the end of 2008 meant there were no price pressures in early 2009. Thus, we were maybe the first country in which the euro was adopted without consumers perceiving any price increases. Had we not adopted the euro in 2009, we would not have been able to meet the Maastricht criteria for the next 4 to 5 years, as the government deficit increased substantially. You might say we were lucky, but I would rather concur with the great biologist and chemist Louis Pasteur that fortune favours the prepared. Shortly after our entry, Slovakia and the rest of the euro area were faced with the most severe financial crisis in European history. The measures taken by the Eurosystem were unprecedented and the easing cycle that started in 2008 is only now coming to an end. Outside of Japan, this is probably the longest easing cycle in the history of central banking. The euro, now twenty years old, can certainly be described as a mature currency. It has survived some very hard times and is now much more resilient. It must be said  especially in this country  that many of the institutional arrangements developed in the euro area in the past decade are making the common currency stronger. Perhaps we were not aware we needed the new arrangements, or perhaps we did not like the costs and effort needed, but these costs should be seen as a form of insurance against future crises. It is better to be insured Narodna banka Slovenska, Imricha Karvasa 1, 813 25 Bratislava, Slovak Republic than not to be  and it is even better to be paying just the insurance premium than to be forced to draw the insurance benefits. I am sure the future will bring further important challenges. I will be keeping my fingers crossed that all my colleagues and future governors at the National Bank of Slovakia manage to meet them. Perhaps there will be another gathering here ten years from now to discuss how views have changed after using the euro for 20 years. One person who knows a thing or two about what 20 years of the euro is like is Mr Yves Mersch, who will be taking the floor shortly. Ladies and gentlemen, I hope you enjoy the conference and contribute to a fruitful discussion. I am very happy to see all of you here. Thank you for your attention. Narodna banka Slovenska, Imricha Karvasa 1, 813 25 Bratislava, Slovak Republic

Title: Closing remarks - Tenth anniversary of the euro in Slovakia
Subtitle: Closing remarks by Mr udovit Odor, Deputy Governor of the National Bank of Slovakia, at the International Conference to mark the tenth anniversary of the introduction of the euro in Slovakia, Bratislava, 11 January 2019.
text: _____________________________________________________________ Narodna banka Slovenska Communication Section CLOSING REMARKS by Mr udovit odor, Deputy Governor of Narodna banka Slovenska at the conference 10 YEARS OF THE URO IN SLOVAKIA International Conference to Mark the 10th Anniversary of the Introduction of the Euro in Slovakia Bratislava, 11 January 2019 Ladies and gentlemen, Let me begin by thanking all the conference speakers and participants for frank and lively discussions. Usually at such anniversaries everybody says everything is fine and the future is bright, but these discussions were really balanced, and I liked that. We talked about opportunities, but also about some possible problems in the future. I will try to summarise the main messages from my point of view. The first issue is the euro itself. When talking about the euro, we heard that its not just an economic concept, but also a political project. Some called themselves proud members of the euro area. So, its not just about economic numbers. If we look back at the things said before the creation of the euro, they included some very pessimistic projections. For example, Milton Friedman gave it ten years at the most. Other voices, however, were very optimistic about the common currency. They expected a huge increase in trade and an endogenous convergence effect. They said that while the euro area may not be the best or an optimal currency union, once countries joined it, they would endogenously converge towards each other. Today, after twenty years, we see something in between these opposite views. Turning to the euro adoption strategy, it was made clear in the presentations that the strategy in Slovakia was very ambitious. When the central bank and Finance Ministry began talks on this issue in 2003, we were light years away from fulfilling all the Maastricht criteria. In the end, the decision to seek euro adoption was a good one and the timing of the adoption was also excellent. Of course, we were lucky to some extent, but thats part of life. As regards the strategy, it was noted today how Slovakia benefited from the euro even before adopting it. Euro preparations acted as a catalyst for structural reforms and public finance consolidation Narodna banka Slovenska, Imricha Karvasa 1, 813 25 Bratislava, Slovak Republic strategies, and they also changed how Slovakia was perceived within the European Union. As was noted today, the road to fulfilling the criteria was a little bit bumpy. Slovakia had previously been on a floating exchange rate, so the major issues included the sustainability of the inflation criterion and the exchange rate pass-through to prices. But the discussions were frank and turned out successful. In terms of the technical issues and the technical changeover, the euro adoption was much less bumpy. Im glad that although we took some its profits, the banking industry is very happy with the euro adoption. The same goes for the citizens and firms, and no major political party is explicitly against it, either. The euro adoption in Slovakia is praised mainly for supporting exchange rate stability, ease of travel, and business. That is pleasing, because it has not been the case in each country that adopted the euro. Several participants stressed that Slovakia could be a role model for countries joining the euro in the future. It was good to hear this from distinguished international economists, and even better to hear it from a Czech economist. Now the question is how we should look at the euro per se. The euro is not a guarantee of prosperity, not something that automatically makes you richer once you adopt it. The common currency is not a blank cheque. Its very important to bear in mind that there are good examples and bad examples. It is not set in stone whether you will prosper or struggle after entering the euro area. Other policies are extremely important. When a country joins the euro area, it gives up the exchange rate as a demand stabilisation tool, so it should prepare other policies to fight against asymmetric shocks, including macroprudential, fiscal, labour market and other structural policies. Today we saw a very lively discussion about the future of the common currency. I really liked the point that we should not see the euro as a blame game between European institutions and Member States. Everybody should understand that its kind a of a shared responsibility. We should try hard to figure out how to reform our governance framework in order to incentivise European institutions, as well as the Member States themselves, to see the euro as a common concern. We talked a little bit about the potential next recession and crisis. We heard how the policy space is more limited now than before the previous crisis. On the other hand, some more optimistic points were made: for example, the banking sector is in much better shape now than before the last recession. What we didnt discuss, but in my view is crucial to the euro areas shock-absorbing capacity, are private risk-sharing channels. Here the discussion about the capital markets union is very important. Towards the end, some speakers stressed that when we have problems, we sometimes discuss and see things from a limited perspective, and that it is very important not to lose sight of the broader picture. The euro area is not just a collection of member states, but a big economic player in the world. We should therefore also try to respond to the shocks coming from global issues, such as trade wars or major productivity trends. Narodna banka Slovenska, Imricha Karvasa 1, 813 25 Bratislava, Slovak Republic Today we heard a lot of interesting ideas in many areas. I opened my presentation earlier today by mentioning my son who is now ten years old. But I also have an older daughter, and I know that the next ten years are usually much more difficult than the first ten. When I look at the twenty-year history of the euro, the same also applies; nevertheless, I dont think the trend is uniform, so I hope that Slovakia will continue being a successful euro area member over the next ten years. Thank you for your attention and your contributions. Narodna banka Slovenska, Imricha Karvasa 1, 813 25 Bratislava, Slovak Republic

Title: Introductory word  at the Conference of Governors of the central banks of the V4 countries in Budapest on the challenges of climate change
text: Tasks of NBS (/) Monetary Counti on of the Co un t ion o f erencii guvernero v central nych banc krajin V4 v Budapesti opveliztions aach v in the context of climate change 16. 7. 2021 Good afternoon . Thank you for inviting me to this debate and it is a pleasure to be here today . It would be even better to be in Budapest in person... it is a pity that we could only meet virtually due to the current situation. Today's topic is the gradual transition to a greener economy. Dornbusch's Law says that "the arrival of a crisis takes much longer than we think, but then it occurs much faster than we would expect," ... it was a case of the pandemic... and I fear that the same scenario could easily occur with climate change. The recent crisis has shown us how fragile our existence is and how a local problem emerging on the other side of the globe can turn into a global one in the blink of an eye. Climate change, like viruses, does not affect just one region, borders, ideology or currency. Greenhouse gases do not affect only one geographical area. They spread everywhere and cause damage to the entire planet. No exceptions and no questions asked. Such global problems require global solutions. No single actor can solve this problem alone. There is now a scientific consensus that climate change poses a serious threat to humanity and the economy. Industrialisation and globalisation are leading to an increase in emissions. However, we are still wondering how to deal effectively with the risks of physical change and the transition to a greener economy. Policies aimed at mitigating and adapting to climate change could trigger a revolution  a sustainable revolution with the potential to shape the world. The carbon budget to keep warming below 2C under the Paris Agreement will be exhausted in about 25 years. Our advantage is that we know that climate change is irreversible. Trillion-dollar investments will be needed to transition the global economy to zero emissions and avert a climate catastrophe. Just as industrial revolutions required the influx of capital and the development of technology. This represents a huge challenge for mobilising capital and a great opportunity for investors to finance new technologies and invest in the business models of the future. We need to change the direction of economic forces in order to create strong incentives (drivers) to encourage investment in research and development, to mobilise public and private capital, and to implement policies to adapt and mitigate the negative consequences of the climate crisis. We need to get rid of obstacles. And what are the positives? Transformation brings growth, jobs and innovation. Climate change as a negative externality is a textbook example of market failure. Financial market supervision Financial stability Banknotes and coins Payments statistika Research Legislation Publications Or national bank Information for media NBS press releases Governments have the most powerful tools at their disposal  carbon pricing, a carbon tax and tradable emission permits. Of course, central banks also have a role to play here within their mandate. Central banks can help to understand the intricacies of this issue, thus avoiding underestimating the possible consequences. And all this before it's too late. More than speeches, we need agreement on common measures to build a sustainable and resilient economy for future generations. We are facing a critical moment; our actions in the next ten years will determine our future. The toll of inaction is increasing every moment, and we must not close our eyes to climate challenges. Today's hustle and bustle has an impact on future generations. There will be no escape. There is no miracle cure. Let us join forces with the best brains in the world and look for acceptable solutions. A voluntary approach is not enough. This brings me to the conclusions of our strategic review last week. We, the Governing Council of the ECB, are aware that climate change has a profound impact on price stability and have therefore committed ourselves to an ambitious climate action plan within the scope of the ECB's mandate . First, we will further expand our analytical capacity in macroeconomic modelling and develop statistical indicators and new tools to assess the effects of climate change on the transmission of monetary policy and on price stability. Second, the ECB will introduce environmental sustainability disclosure requirements as a presumption of eligibility for collateral and asset purchases. Third, we are adapting our risk assessment system, corporate sector asset purchases and collateral framework to take climate risks into account. The implementation of the Action Plan will be in line with the progress of EU policies and initiatives on environmental sustainability disclosure and reporting, including the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive , the Taxonomy Regulation and regulations on sustainability-related disclosures in the financial services sector. I will end with the words of President Lagarde: 'We do not drive the bus, but we do ride in it. ... it's not just talk ... it is the commitment of the entire Governing Council to act and it is a huge step forward. Things have already started to move." Conference recording NBS Governor Peter Kazimir from 24:27. Title: NBS expert: Up to 80 percent of fraud can be detected with simple steps (Jlia illkov for HN)
text: NBS Expert: Possible up to 80 percentage of fraud can be seen through using simple steps (Julia illikova for HN) Dec 9, 2022 Katarina selestiakova In an interview with HN, Julia illikova, Executive Director of the Financial Consumer Supervision and Protection Department of the National Bank of Slovakia, says, among other things:  The Internet and virtual space is a ready-made well of various sophisticated Fraud.  We do not excel in financial literacy, which is also what the submissions tell us financial consumers.  Being educated and alert, not making "schoolboy" mistakes can save our heads in sadness.  It is the task of the state to take compensatory measures, especially for low-income households, so that they do not get into even greater financial problems.  The adage "high potential return equals high risk of loss" still applies, no matter who tries to convince you otherwise. It is common knowledge that people in Slovakia have a low level of financial literacy. Why is that? I'm a math physicist and I like exact numbers. And maybe that's where my sentiment comes from, that we in Slovakia don't have many of those accurate and fresh numbers. Therefore, we were left with the feeling that we do not excel in financial literacy, which is also what the submissions tell us financial consumers, which are often a sad picture of reality and financial "illiteracy". This is also evidenced by the data from the latest financial literacy measurements in which the inhabitants of Slovakia participated. Which measurements are you talking about? First of all, PISA2018, which is a measurement for 15-year-old pupils. The results showed that they are below the OECD average and compared to the measurement in 2015, some countries have missed us even more. The same applies to the latest, but really quite old OECD Programme for the International Assessment of Adult Competences - PIAAC, in which we last joined In 2012, the result was unflattering. It is a pity that our answer to PISA2018 was not to participate in the next survey in 2021. We didn't get involved because no one wants to see more bad results. And what is actually the reason that the children ended up below average in the measurements? It is difficult to assume that if we are below average in reading and mathematical literacy, we will be great in financial literacy. A lot has been said about the systemic solution There was a discussion in society, but we saw from consumer complaints that not much had moved. That's why we decided about two years ago not to wait for anyone and launch a financial education project under the 5money brand. We will come back to the project later, but I would like to know if the financial literacy contributes to the fact that Slovaks so often fall for fraudsters. We could talk about naivety, credulity, the desire to get rich quickly, the inclination to believe in hoaxes, but I explain it mainly by low financial literacy. Best The consumer protector is himself an educated and well-rounded consumer. In your opinion, the victims of fraudsters are mostly older people? Based on our experience from submissions, fraudsters "tailor-made" frauds for individual target groups. Older people are attracted to other "products", young people who are looking for yield and adventure to others. But we can say with certainty that seniors belong to a more vulnerable group, and therefore in our project We concentrate 5 money. Where can seniors seek your advice? We are currently working together through the Union of Pensioners Slovakia, we try to cooperate with local governments and we also use classic communication channels such as radio, television and education, which is a very good Prevention. We are also trying to get involved in the Digital Seniors project, because the Internet And the virtual space is a ready-made well of various sophisticated scams. However, I would not underestimate the fraud on the rest of the population either. Be educated And be alert, not making "schoolboy" mistakes can save our heads in sadness. Do we think so, or has the number of frauds really increased during the covid pandemic? Yes. Computer security firms report that the number of phishing scams, for example, has doubled in the past year. Quarantine and the transfer of purchases to the virtual space have brought chances for fraudsters. Suddenly, there were people on the Internet who had no experience with buying over the Internet, providing data about the card and were too gullible. We have also noticed an increase in fraud in client complaints. Scams are also evolving, becoming more sophisticated. While in the year  there were only eight submissions in the case of payment card fraud or phishing, in 2010  That was 54 submissions and this year we have already registered 79 submissions. At the same time, our numbers they are not talking about the number of frauds, but about the number of submissions we have received at the NBS. We should not forget that victims of such scams feel frustrated, ashamed and very often do not even admit to their own family. However, shame is not appropriate. How does a payment card be misused? Perpetrators assume inattention and take advantage of the ignorance of payment card holders. They pose as alleged courier services, customs clearances, and fake payment gateways. Let me remind you that a payment card cannot be accepted, unlike an account. And if a payment card is really misused, it is necessary to block it immediately and prevent further losses. I also recommend filing a criminal complaint. Although it is fair to add that the hope of returning the stolen money is minimal. Apparently, people are probably lazy to read contracts. However, what types of scams are currently the most widespread? At the beginning of the pandemic, these were less sophisticated scams - almost everyone expected some kind of shipment. People revealed, or entered their data or security features, and instead of an amount of, for example, 4.50 euros, which was supposed to be a delivery fee, they went from the account of 450 euros, sometimes repeatedly. The victim is given a fake link, and if she doesn't click on it, nothing happens. The post office or similar courier companies never ask payment of some transport costs in advance via links in SMS or e-mails. Another type of fraud is sales, for example, through online bazaars. Scams work on the principle that you sell something, such as a mobile phone, and the buyer claims to send you money to your card. This form of transfer - directly to a payment card - Does not exist. Money can only be sent to an account, so it is standard to provide a bank account - IBAN, and not card data and its security features. Isn't it the case that banks catch these scams and warn clients in advance? In the case of fraud such as GooglePay/ApplePay, if the fraudster catches the security features, he can install these applications on his mobile phone and "cheerfully" pays. What is striking here is that almost all banks, before registering a request to install these "wallets", send a warning that says something like: "We have just noticed that you want to install Google Pay/Apple Pay. If it's not you, please contact us immediately." Nevertheless, many clients will make authorization elements available to crooks to install. Over time, scammers want more and more, trying to gain access to internet banking, they transfer entire balances, even make a transfer from a savings account to a current account and transfer all the money. We also recorded the acceptance of an offer for a pre-approved loan. How do fraudsters get access to that data? Fraudsters most often obtain data by slipping a fake e-mail or SMS that pretends to be from the bank, or calling as "employees" of the bank, and the phone actually shows that the caller is the bank. Or simply people click on a fraudulent link and allow hackers to access a computer or internet banking. And there are still totally unsophisticated inheritance scams, spouses and the like, which promise that if you send them a certain amount of money, everything will work out for the good He will turn around, and you will be rich and healthy. Is there any simple advice - how not to fall for it? Another relatively unsophisticated, but often occurring "product" is the opportunity to earn terribly quickly and terribly profitably, and if you don't make a quick decision, you will lose this never-repeating chance. The lesson is simple - if someone offers you something above average and also says how lucky you are that this offer came to you, it is wise to pay attention and check it out. In HN, we recently wrote about the fact that the National Bank of Slovakia is also being abused by fraudsters in the sense that its logo or name is used as bait for clients. How can this be prevented? Not even the National Bank can avoid the fact that someone is unjustifiably hiding behind it, And such cases are increasing. It is the same as when some scammers claim that "profitable investment" is protected by the World Bank, and similar logical nonsense. The best defense is to be a literate consumer. He knows that central banks are not classic commercial banks, nor are the World Bank, or the BIS, and the like, banks that offer banking services to individuals. When we see this, it is worth paying attention again. It is also very useful to think before Any action you take with an institution that claims to be a licensed financial institution, check it against our register of supervised entities. You can find it on the website subjekty.nbs.sk. If a company is not on the list, it is a signal that there may be a problem somewhere. Equally useful advice is to look up if anyone has had a negative experience with a similar situation. Indeed, just a few minutes and a moment of your attention can very easily and quickly prevent huge problems. Perhaps up to 80 percent of frauds can be seen through with very simple steps. Doesn't such misuse of the logo and name reduce the authority of the National Bank? If we look at it through this lens, fraudsters are constantly reducing the authority of various institutions. But now seriously. Whenever there is similar activity, we try to post a warning on our site. Therefore, if you have any suspicions, check to see if you can find a similar warning on the NBS website. Of course, we always consider taking appropriate legal action, carrying out supervision, but oversight is non-public and therefore we do not inform the public during the process. However, it is true that a consumer with at least basic financial literacy has a huge chance of seeing through most of these scams. In an interview, you said that "Slovaks don't know about money, we don't have much to be proud of." However, you are also involved in consumer protection, how many complaints have you received over the years? Is their number growing? I have already mentioned that Slovaks are not familiar with money and their financial literacy has long been below the average of OECD countries. In addition, the submissions we receive are only a fraction of the statistics of bad decisions, but unfortunately, we do not have others yet. The number of submissions is relatively stable, we have been receiving about two thousand a year for a long time. Last year, we have seen a slight decline and we have 1,500 submissions so far this year. At first glance, it may seem that the number of complaints has been decreasing over the past year, but this is mainly caused by the pandemic period, when people complained less. Unfortunately, our data They say that many clients still do not understand financial services, they have false expectations and also easily fall victim to scammers. Is it worth complaining to people? Is there a remedy after filing a complaint? What changes over time is the structure of the sectors to which the submissions relate. Only less than a third of the submissions we receive at the NBS every year are justified. These are submissions where NBS has found a violation of generally binding legal regulations or contractual agreements. In more than half of such cases, the financial institution voluntarily proceeds to remedy the situation after our intervention. As part of the remedy, financial institutions returned more than 400 thousand euros to clients annually. What do Slovaks complain about most often in your country? They are dissatisfied, for example, With insurance companies, with banking services? In principle, the structure of the sectors changes depending on the "hot topics". The submitted submissions basically copy reality, for example, in 2015, when the NBS took over the supervision of the "non-banknotes", these were submissions related to consumer loans they provide. At the beginning of the pandemic, these were mainly submissions regarding deferrals of installments. During pandemic, there were fewer submissions related to insufficient performance by insurance companies in compensation for damage from health insurance or accident insurance, as there were fewer driving - in 2021, there were the fewest traffic accidents since the establishment of Slovakia. By default, many submissions are directed against the charging of fees by banks and the failure to provide sufficient information before entering into a contractual relationship, these submissions concern basically all sectors. Indebted households are also a problem, do you monitor whether they are successful in repaying their loans or whether they have applied for a deferral of repayments? What data do you have on this? It is clear from our numbers that the credit quality of loans received by consumers in Slovakia has been stable for a long time. This means that despite the recent covid pandemic and now increased inflation, households are able to repay their loans. The default rate of housing loans has been very close to zero for a long time. So if clients get into problems with mortgage repayment, they can find a solution with the bank. In the case of consumer loans, The loan default rate is currently below two percent, which is also not bad. Is the economic crisis and its impact on households already visible? For example in the number of non-performing loans? From our data, we can see that the increase in energy prices and inflation are not currently reflected in the default of consumer loans. However, from analyses and simulations, we conclude that Households are most vulnerable to rising inflation. We have a group of vulnerable households that will depreciate in the event of long-term high inflation without compensation for depreciation real income can get into trouble paying their mortgage. That's why At the NBS, we believe that it is the task of the state to adopt compensatory measures at this time, especially for low-income households, also so that they do not get into even larger financial problems. We have one hundred percent deposit protection up to a relatively high threshold. Is it a good step? Doesn't this make it easier for people to handle money? The Deposit Protection Fund is a regulation resulting from European regulation. In some circles, there is a debate whether guarantees do not create a so-called moral hazard, when the consumer does not take responsibility for his decision, but relies on guarantee schemes. It should be noted that banking products, traditional bank deposits, are probably the most well-known and most used products from the client's point of view. If the client verifies, for example in our register, that the bank offering the product is actually licensed and supervised, the risk is minimal. Most problems arise when the client forgets that a high promised return means a much higher risk of loss. For example, let's compare an annual term deposit in a bank, protected by a deposit protection fund, where the average yield is currently somewhere around one percent and for a long time they were at zero with an attractive offer of investments with a yield incomparably more attractive. Here it is necessary to pay attention and carefully evaluate the risk of loss. Because the maxim "high potential return equals high risk of loss" still applies, no matter who tries to convince you otherwise. In the introduction, you mentioned the 5money project several times. What are your outputs and feedback from this project on the effectiveness of the campaign? Our 5money project is not just a campaign, but a comprehensive long-term project to increase financial literacy for everyone, i.e. for children, students, adults and seniors, and we do not forget about particularly vulnerable groups. About two years ago, we They said that we are not waiting for anyone anymore and we will put our hand to work. We have a clear idea and also specific steps and activities that are aimed at individual groups of the population. We are trying to make our brand known to more and more residents of Slovakia, but each of our communication is education. We have a "learning first" approach. Outputs from the project 5 money is free for the public. We want to take advantage of the trust that the NBS has and we would like to use the 5money brand to cover meaningful educational projects. We are looking for partners who do a good job, have quality projects. We want to be a kind of umbrella in the field of financial education. Who is Julia illikova Julia illikova is the Executive Director of the Financial Consumer Supervision and Protection Division of the National Bank of Slovakia. After graduating from the Faculty of Mathematics, Physics and Informatics, she worked at the Ministry of Finance, where in 1999 she became the head of supervision of insurance. He also represents the National Bank of Slovakia in various international institutions.
text_original: Odbornka NBS: Mono a 80 percent podvodov sa d prekukn pomocou jednoduchch krokov (Jlia illkov pre HN) 9. dec 2022 Katarna elestiakov Vkonn riaditeka seku dohadu a ochrany finannch spotrebiteov Nrodnej banky Slovenska Jlia illkov v rozhovore pre HN okrem inho hovor:  Internet a virtulny priestor je hotovou studnicou rzne sofistikovanch podvodov.  Vo finannej gramotnosti nevynikme, o om nm hovoria aj podania finannch spotrebiteov.  By vzdelan a v strehu, nerobi kolcke chyby nm me uetri hlavu v smtku.  Je lohou ttu prijma kompenzan opatrenia najm pre nzkoprjmov domcnosti, aby sa nedostali ete do vch finannch problmov.  Pouka vysok potencilny vnos sa rovn vysok riziko straty stle plat, nech sa vs ktokovek bude snai presvedi o inom. Je veobecne znme, e udia na Slovensku maj nzku rove finannej gramotnosti. Preo je to tak? Som matfyzka a mm rada presn sla. A mono z toho vychdza mj sentiment, e my na Slovensku vea tch presnch a erstvch sel nemme. Preto nm zostal len pocit, e vo finannej gramotnosti nevynikme, o om nm hovoria aj podania finannch spotrebiteov, ktor s asto smutnm obrazom reality a finannej negramotnosti. Hovoria o tom aj daje z poslednch meran finannej gramotnosti, na ktorch sa obyvatelia Slovenska zastnili. O ktorch meraniach hovorte? Predovetkm PISA2018, o je meranie u 15-ronch iakov. Vsledky ukzali, e s pod priemerom OECD a oproti meraniu v roku 2015 nm niektor krajiny ete viac uli. Rovnako v poslednom, ale u naozaj dos starom OECD Programe medzinrodnho hodnotenia kompetenci dospelch - PIAAC, do ktorho sme sa naposledy zapojili v roku 2012, bol vsledok nelichotiv. koda, e naou odpoveou na PISA2018 bolo nezapoji sa do alieho prieskumu v roku 2021. Nezapojili sme sa, lebo nikto asi nechce vidie alie zl vsledky. A o je vlastne tm dvodom, e deti v meraniach skonili podpriemerne? Je ak predpoklada, e ke sme podpriemern v itateskej a matematickej gramotnosti, tak budeme super vo finannej gramotnosti. O systmovom rieen sa vea v spolonosti diskutovalo, ale my sme na sanostiach spotrebiteov videli, e sa vea nepohlo. Preto sme sa rozhodli zhruba pred dvoma rokmi neaka na nikoho a rozbehn projekt finannho vzdelvania pod znakou 5peaz. K tomu projektu sa ete vrtime, ma by vak zaujmalo, i sa prve nzka finann gramotnos podpisuje pod fakt, e Slovci tak asto naletia podvodnkom. Mohli by sme hovori o naivite, dverivosti, tbe rchlo zbohatn, nklonnosti veri hoaxom, aleja si to vysvetujem najm nzkou finannou gramotnosou. Najlep ochranca spotrebitea je sm vzdelan a rozhaden spotrebite. S poda vs obeami podvodnkov zva star udia? Pokia vychdzam z naich sksenost z podan, podvodnci ij na mieru podvody jednotlivm cieovm skupinm. Starch ud lkaj na in produkty, mladch ud, ktor hadaj vnos a dobrodrustvo, zas na in. Ale s uritosou meme poveda, e seniori patria medzi viac ohrozen skupinu, a preto sa na nich v naom projekte 5peaz sstreujeme. Kde si seniori mu vyhada vae rady? Momentlne mme rozbehnut spoluprcu prostrednctvom Jednoty dchodcov Slovenska, sname sa spolupracova so samosprvami a vyuvame aj klasick komunikan kanly ako rozhlas, televziu a vzdelvanie, ktor je vemi dobrou prevenciou. Tie sa sname zapoji do projektu Digitlni seniori, pretoe internet a virtulny priestor je hotovou studnicou rzne sofistikovanch podvodov. Nepodceovala by som vak ani podvody na ostatnej populcii. By vzdelan a v strehu, nerobi kolcke chyby nm me uetri hlavu v smtku. Zd sa nm to alebo naozaj vzrstol poet podvodov poas pandmie covidu? no. Firmy, ktor sa zaoberaj potaovou bezpenosou, hlsia, e za uplynul rok vzrstol naprklad poet phishingovch podvodov a dvojnsobne. Karantna a presun nkupov do virtulneho priestoru priniesli pre podvodnkov ance. Na internete sa zrazu ocitli udia, ktor nemali sksenosti s nkupom cez internet, poskytovanm dajov o karte a boli privemi dveriv. Nrast podvodov sme zaznamenali aj my v sanostiach klientov. Podvody sa tie vyvjaj, s oraz sofistikovanejie. Km v roku 2020 bolo len osem podan vo veci zneuitia platobnej karty alebo phishingu, v roku 2021 to bol 54 podan a v tomto roku evidujeme u 79 podan. Nae sla pritom nehovoria o pote podvodov, ale pote podan, ktor sme v NBS dostali. Nemali by sme zabudn, e obete takchto podvodov sa ctia frustrovan, hanbia sa a vemi asto sa nepriznaj ani vlastnej rodine. Hanba vak nie je namieste. Ako dochdza k zneuitiu platobnej karty? Pchatelia predpokladaj nepozornos a vyuvaj nevedomos majiteov platobnch kariet. Vydvaj sa za dajn kurirske sluby, coln konania a falon platobn brny. Pripomeniem, e na platobn kartu sa ned, na rozdiel od tu, prija platba. A ak u naozaj prde k zneuitiu platobnej karty, je potrebn, aby sme ju okamite zablokovali a zabrnili tm alm stratm. Odporam tie poda trestn oznmenie. Aj ke je fr doda, e ndej na vrtenie ukradnutch peaz je minimlna. udia s poda vetkho asi leniv ta zmluvy. Ak typy podvodov s vak aktulne najrozrenejie? Na zaiatku pandmie ilo o menej sofistikovan podvody - takmer kad oakval nejak zsielku. udia vyzradili, respektve zadali svoje daje i bezpenostn prvky a namiesto sumy naprklad 4,50 eura, o mal by poplatok za doruenie, im odilo z tu 450 eur, niekedy aj opakovane. Obeti je podsunut falon link, a keby na neklikla, tak sa ni nedeje. Pota a ani podobn kurirske spolonosti nikdy neptaj vopred zaplatenie nejakch dopravnch nkladov cez odkazy v SMS alebo mailoch. alm typom podvodov je predaj naprklad prostrednctvom online bazrov. Podvody funguj na princpe, e nieo predvate, naprklad mobil, priom kupujci tvrd, e vm peniaze pole na vau kartu. Takto forma prevodu - priamo na platobn kartu - neexistuje. Peniaze sa daj odosla iba na et, preto je tandardn poskytn bankov spojenie - IBAN, a nie daje z karty a jej bezpenostn prvky. Nie je to tak, e banky tieto podvody zachytia a klientov vopred varuj? Pri podvodoch typu GooglePay/ApplePay, ak podvodnk odchyt bezpenostn prvky, vie si sm intalova tieto aplikcie u vo svojom mobilnom telefne a veselo plat. Tu je zarajce, e takmer vetky banky pred tm, ako zaeviduj iados o intalovanie tchto peaeniek, zasielaj upozornenie, ktor hovor nieo ako: Prve sme zaznamenali, e chcete intalova Google Pay/Apple Pay. Ak to nie ste vy, okamite ns kontaktujte. Napriek tomu mnoho klientov podvodnkom sprstupn autorizan prvky na intalciu. Postupom asu chc podvodnci oraz viac, snaia sa zska prstup do internetbankingu, presvaj cel zostatky, dokonca aj urobia prevod zo sporiaceho tu na ben et a preved vetky peniaze. Zaznamenali sme aj akceptovanie ponuky na predschvlen ver. Akm spsobom sa k tm dtam podvodnci dostvaj? Podvodnci najastejie zskaj daje tak, e podsun falon mail alebo SMS, ktor sa tvria, e s z banky, alebo volaj ako zamestnanci banky a na telefne sa skutone zobraz, e volajcim je banka. Alebo jednoducho udia klikn na podvodn link a umonia hackerom prstup k potau, respektve k internetbankingu. No a ete stle sa objavuj totlne nesofistikovan podvody s dedistvom, manelmi a podobne, ktor subuj, e ak im polete nejak sumu peaz, vetko sa na dobr obrti a vy budete bohat a zdrav. Je nejak jednoduch rada - ako nenaletie? alm pomerne nesofistikovanm, ale asto sa vyskytujcim produktom je monos strane rchlo a strane vhodne zarobi, a pokia sa nerozhodnete rchlo, tak o tto nikdy sa neopakujcu ancu prdete. Pouenie je jednoduch - ak vm niekto ponka nieo nadpriemerne vhodn a ete aj hovor, ak mte astie, e tto ponuka prila k vm, je rozumn spozornie a preveri si to. V HN sme nedvno psali o tom, e aj Nrodn banka Slovenska sa podvodnkmi zneuva v tom zmysle, e jej logo i nzov sa pouva ako nvnada na klientov. Ako sa d tomu brni? Ani Nrodn banka sa nevyhne tomu, e sa za u niekto neoprvnene skrva, a takchto prpadov pribda. Je to rovnak, ako ke niektor podvodnci tvrdia, e vhodn investcia je chrnen Svetovou bankou, a podobn logick nezmysly. Najlepia obrana je by gramotn spotrebite. Ten vie, e centrlne banky nie s klasickmi komernmi bankami, podobne ani Svetov banka, prpadne BIS a podobne nie s banky, ktor ponkaj bankov sluby pre jednotlivcov. Ke to vidme, optovne sa oplat spozornie. Rovnako je vemi uiton si pred akmkovek krokom s intitciou, ktor sa vydva za licencovan finann intitciu, skontrolova si ju v naom registri dohliadanch subjektov. Njdete ho na strnke subjekty.nbs.sk. Ak sa spolonos v zozname nenachdza, je signl, e niekde me by problm. Rovnako uitonou radou je vyhada si, i s podobnou situciou nem niekto negatvne sksenosti. Naozaj len pr mint a chvka vaej pozornosti mu vemi ahko a rchlo preds obrovskm problmom. Mono a 80 percent podvodov sa d prekukn pomocou vemi jednoduchch krokov. Nezniuje takto zneuvanie loga a mena autoritu Nrodnej banky? Ak by sme sa na to pozerali touto optikou, tak podvodnci sstavne zniuj autoritu rznych intitci. Ale teraz vne. Vdy, ke sa objav podobn aktivita, sname sa zverejni varovanie na naej strnke. Preto ak mte podozrenie, pozrite sa, i aj na strnke NBS u podobn varovanie nenjdete. Samozrejme, vdy zvaujeme podniknutie prslunch prvnych krokov, vykonanie dohadu, ale dohad je neverejn, a preto verejnos poas procesu neinformujeme. No plat, e spotrebite disponujci aspo zkladnou finannou gramotnosou m obrovsk ancu vinu tchto podvodov prekukn. V jednom rozhovore ste povedali, e Slovci sa nevyznaj v peniazoch, nemme by vemi na o pyn. Venujete sa vak aj ochrane spotrebitea, koko sanost ste za roky dostali? Rastie ich poet? To, e sa Slovci nevyznaj v peniazoch a ich finann gramotnos je dlhodobo pod priemerom krajn OECD, som u spomnala. Navye, podania, ktor nm prichdzaj, s len zlomok tatistk zlch rozhodnut, ale in, ia, zatia nemme. Poet podan je pomerne stabiln, dlhodobo ich dostvame okolo dvetisc rone. Minul rok sme zaznamenali mierny pokles a tento rok mme zatia 1 500 podan. Na prv pohad sa me zda, e poet sanost sa za posledn rok zniuje, no je to vyvolan predovetkm obdobm pandmie, ke sa udia saovali menej. ia, nae dta hovoria o tom, e mnoh klienti stle nerozumej finannm slubm, maj od nich nesprvne oakvania a tie sa ahko stvaj obeami podvodnkov. Oplat sa uom saova? Dochdza po podan sanosti aj k nprave? To, o sa v ase men, je truktra sektorov, ktorch sa podania tkaj. Len necel tretina podan, ktor v NBS kadorone dostvame, je opodstatnen. Ide o podania, kde NBS kontatovala poruenie veobecne zvznch prvnych predpisov alebo zmluvnch dohd. Vo viac ako polovici takchto prpadov pristpi finann intitcia po naej intervencii dobrovone k nprave. Finann intitcie v rmci prijatia npravy vrtili klientom rone viac ako 400-tisc eur. Na o sa Slovci u vs najastejie sauj? S nespokojn naprklad s poisovami, s bankovmi slubami? truktra sektorov sa v princpe men v zvislosti od horcich tm. Doruen podania v podstate kopruj realitu, naprklad v roku 2015, ke NBS prevzala dohad nad nebankovkami, to boli podania tkajce sa spotrebiteskch verov, ktor poskytuj. Zaiatkom pandmie to boli hlavne podania tkajce sa odkladov spltok. Poas pandmie bolo menej podan, ktor sa tkali nedostatonho plnenia zo strany poisovn pri nhrade kody z PZP alebo havarijnho poistenia, kee sa menej jazdilo - za rok 2021 bolo najmenej dopravnch nehd od vzniku Slovenska. tandardne vea podan smeruje voi tovaniu poplatkov zo strany bnk a neposkytnutiu dostatonch informci pred vstupom do zmluvnho vzahu, tieto podania sa tkaj v podstate vetkch sektorov. Problmom s aj zadlen domcnosti, sledujete, i sa im dar splca very alebo i poiadali o odklad spltok? Ak mte o tom daje? Z naich sel je zrejm, e na Slovensku je dlhodobo stabiln kreditn kvalita verov, ktor dostvaj spotrebitelia. Znamen to, e napriek nedvnej pandmii covidu a teraz aj zvenej inflcii s domcnosti schopn splca svoje very. Miera zlyhania verov na bvanie je dlhodobo vemi blzka nule. Take ak sa klienti dostan do problmov so splcanm hypotky, doku s bankou njs rieenie. Pri spotrebiteskch veroch je miera nesplcania verov aktulne pod dve percent, o tie nie je zl. Je u viditen ekonomick krza a jej dosahy na domcnosti? Naprklad v mnostve zlyhanch verov? Z naich dt vidme, e zvenie cien energi a inflcia sa aktulne neprejavuje na zlyhanosti verov spotrebiteov. Z analz a zo simulci nm vak vychdza, e domcnosti s najviac zraniten voi zvyujcej sa inflcii. Mme skupinu zranitench domcnost, ktor sa pri dlhodobo vysokej inflcii bez kompenzcie znehodnotenia relnych prjmov mu dosta do problmov so splcanm svojej hypotky. Preto si v NBS myslme, e je lohou ttu prijma v tomto ase kompenzan opatrenia najm pre nzkoprjmov domcnosti, a to aj preto, aby sa nedostali ete do vch finannch problmov. Mme tu stopercentn ochranu vkladov po pomerne vysok hranicu. Je to dobr krok? Nezahuje to u ud spsob nakladania s peniazmi? Fond ochrany vkladov je prava vyplvajca z eurpskej regulcie. V niektorch kruhoch sa debatuje, i garancie nevytvraj takzvan morlny hazard, ke spotrebite nepreber zodpovednos za svoje rozhodnutie, ale spolieha sa na garann schmy. Treba si uvedomi, e bankov produkty, tradin bankov vklady, s z pohadu klienta asi najznmejie a najpouvanejie produkty. Ak si klient over, naprklad v naom registri, e banka ponkajca produkt m skutone licenciu a je dohliadan, riziko je minimlne. Vina problmov vznik, ke klient pozabudne, e vysok subovan vnos znamen ovea vyie riziko straty. Naprklad porovnajme si ron termnovan vklad v banke, chrnen fondom ochrany vkladov, kde je momentlne priemern vnos niekde okolo jednho percenta a dlho boli na nule s atraktvnou ponuku investcie s vnosom neporovnatene atraktvnejm. Tu treba spozornie a pozorne vyhodnoti riziko straty. Pretoe pouka vysok potencilny vnos sa rovn vysok riziko straty stle plat, nech sa vs ktokovek bude snai presvedi o inom. V vode ste viackrt spomnali projekt 5peaz. Ak mte z tohto projektu vstupy a sptn vzbu o innosti kampane? N projekt 5peaz nie je len kampa, ale komplexn dlhodob projekt zvyovania finannej gramotnosti pre vetkch, teda pre deti, tudentov, dospelch a po seniorov a nezabdame na obzvl ohrozen skupiny. Pred zhruba dvoma rokmi sme si povedali, e u neakme na nikoho a prilome ruku k dielu. Mme jasn predstavu a aj konkrtne kroky a aktivity, ktor smeruj k jednotlivm skupinm obyvatestva. Sname sa, aby nau znaku poznalo oraz viac obyvateov Slovenska, ale kad naa komunikcia je vzdelvanie. Mme prstup learning first. Vstupy z projektu 5peaz s pre verejnos zadarmo. Chceme vyui dveru, ktor NBS m, a radi by sme znakou 5peaz zastreovali zmyslupln vzdelvacie projekty. Vyhadvame partnerov, ktor robia dobr prcu, maj kvalitn projekty. My chceme by akmsi ddnikom na poli finannho vzdelvania. Kto je Jlia illkov Jlia illkov je vkonn riaditeka seku dohadu a ochrany finannch spotrebiteov Nrodnej banky Slovenska. Po absolvovan Fakulty matematiky, fyziky a informatiky pracovala na ministerstve financi, kde sa v roku 1999 stala vedcou dohadu nad poisovnctvom. Nrodn banku Slovenska zastupuje aj v rznych medzinrodnch intitcich.

Title: Economist ubo Pstor: If gas from Russia stops flowing to Europe, we will probably not avoid a sharp recession (interview of a member of the bank board for HN)
text: Economist ubos Pastor: If by Europe will stop flowing gas from Russia, we probably won't be able to avoid severe recession (interview of a member of the Bank Board for H N) July 4, 2022 Petra Uhrakova  In the interview, you will learn how the current situation resembles the financial crisis of 2008  Whether the war in Ukraine will trigger another global crisis  Whether we should be worried about a recession  What are the reasons behind rising real estate prices In 2008, the world was hit by a financial and subsequently economic crisis. How do you think the situation is similar now and how is it different? I see more differences than similarities. At that time, dubious mortgages and highly indebted banks were mainly a problem. Today, banks are in a much better condition. We also have stricter credit rules and, in general, stricter financial regulations. Therefore, I am not afraid of a return to the crisis of 2008. Today's threats are more of a geopolitical nature. At that time, there was an obvious bubble in real estate prices in the USA, but also in Slovakia. As in previous years, banks competed in attracting people before 2008. Are real estate prices too inflated even now? Real estate prices have really risen sharply. This is mainly due to the long-term low level of interest rates. In addition, we have had rapid growth here in recent years real wages. Both of these factors make it easier for Slovak households to repay mortgage loans. However, after a sharp increase in real estate prices last year, the availability of housing in our country has decreased significantly. Interest rates are also starting to rise and inflation is biting into real wages. Therefore, I expect that the real estate market This year it will get colder. I do not expect a slump, but a slowdown in growth. A slight decline cannot be ruled out either. Do you now expect a recession or even a crisis of the same proportions as after the collapse of Lehman Brothers in 2008? I don't expect a major financial crisis, but an economic slowdown will. It can also come Recession. In the United States, I expect a mild recession already this year or next year, I give it a probability of two to one. The US Fed has already started with a vigorous increase interest rates at a pace, which should slow down the economy with some delay. Another harbinger of a possible recession is a sharp decline in capital markets in the first half of this year. On the other hand, however, the labor market is holding up extremely well, not only in America, but also in our country. Where is the most problematic place in the economy now, which could be crisis, and under what circumstances? I consider the development of the war conflict in Ukraine to be the biggest question mark. If gas from Russia stops flowing to Europe , we will probably not avoid a sharp recession. Especially in Slovakia, as we are extremely dependent on Russian gas. The second question mark is whether the financial markets will be willing to tolerate the high indebtedness of the Italian government. Can recession and crisis be avoided? What steps should be taken? Yes, but we will also need a bit of luck. The effort to avoid a recession is certainly there. Economic policy remains relatively relaxed. Monetary policy in the euro area is starting to tighten, but so far only slowly, and we have a recovery plan. I guess that will be enough. If a recession came, how long could it last? Would it also affect small Slovakia with a very open economy? I don't dare to estimate the duration of something that may not even come. But if a recession comes to Europe, we probably won't avoid it either, as our economy is as open as you say. The situation is also complicated by our extremely high dependence on raw materials from Russia, which puts us in a more fragile situation compared to most Western countries. Central banks have made mistakes in influencing prices in recent years Money? What else should the Fed or the ECB have done? Today's high inflation rate certainly surprised central banks. Looking into the They might have preferred to start tightening monetary policy a few months earlier. But retrospectively evaluating decisions is easier than making them in real time. It is not easy to start tightening monetary policy during a pandemic when Moreover, no one knows how long the pandemic will last. During the pandemic, the public asked how central banks could help the economy, not when they would finally start it delay. It is also important to remember that central banks have a limited ability to tame inflation, which is caused by supply-side shocks. Both covid and the war represented Supply shocks. When there is a shortage of raw materials or food on the market, their prices naturally rise. Central banks can print money, but they can't print oil or grain. Neither unload cargo ships that wait in queues at ports for days. Will high, even double-digit inflation in Slovakia be a reality for only two years? What Will it have consequences for sectors of the economy?  The National Bank of Slovakia currently expects inflation to be slightly above ten percent this year and next, but we expect it to return below three percent soon after. The development of inflation will depend mainly on the development of the war conflict, but also partly on the development of the pandemic and other factors. Inflation should affect industry more than services, as services are less dependent on raw materials such as oil or natural gas.  With inflation of 8 percent, the Fed reacts faster than the ECB. Which strategy is better, is the Fed going into more shock therapy, with the recovery coming sooner? The US Fed is reacting faster because it faces higher inflation. This was partly due to the huge fiscal stimulus in the US during the corona crisis. That stimulus was more or less financed by the creation of new money, as the Fed bought new government bonds that were issued to cover pandemic costs. When you create a lot of new money, give it to the Americans, and they start spending it on a large scale, that's a recipe for inflation. The second reason why the ECB is slower to react is that it has to look not only at inflation, but also at the stability of the eurozone. Unlike the US, we do not have a fiscal union in the eurozone And we still lack stabilising elements, such as common deposit insurance. One would expect that after the European debt crisis of ten years ago, it would happen to complete the security infrastructure in the euro area, but this has not happened. Although we have seen a significant shift, in the end, the ECB remains the main fireman of the euro area. It is therefore forced to monitor not only inflation, but also differences in bond prices in different eurozone countries, especially in its periphery. Therefore, the ECB must be more cautious in tightening monetary policy than the Fed, which does not have to worry about the development of bond prices in Texas or Mississippi.
