Title: Governor P. Kaimr's interview with Bloomberg
text: Rozhovor guvernera P. Kazimira pre agenturu Bloomberg ECBs Kazimir Backs End of QE in August, Flexibility on Hikes  Summer lull would be natural1 timing to conclude purchases  Slovak central bank chief urges new guidance on timing of hike By Peter Laca and Alexander Weber 18. 2. 2022 (Bloomberg)  The European Central Bank should wind down net bond-buying in the summer, while giving itself more flexibility on the timetable for any subsequent interest-rate increase, according to Governing Council member Peter Kazimir. The Slovak central bank chief said the tool  which was created to stave off deflation after Europes debt crisis and was expanded during the pandemic  has outlived its usefulness. The ECB doesnt have a firm end date for its regular purchases, known as APP. The risks this instrument was designed to address have subsided, while on the other hand the negative side effects are becoming more significant," Kazimir said Thursday in an interview. Trading activity weakens in August so that would be a good natural timing for ending the program." Facing unprecedented euro-area inflation, ECB officials have fallen into agreement on the need to pare back support measures that include record-low interest rates and a second bond-buying program deployed when Covid-19 struck and due to end in March. Where they differ is on the speed at which the shift should happen. ECB Governing Council: Hawks & Doves (D Lagarde 0) bo 05 U d w Panetta Lane Schnabel a) Z5 De Cos * (D (3) Villeroy Elderson Guindos Visco Rehn Stournaras * Herodotou * Simkus Wunsch (D Kazimir G Muller Holzmann Kazaks O Vasle c I Doves Neutral Hawks Unrated/lnfrequent Speakers Reinesch Scicluna * No Voting Rights in February Source: Bloomberg Economics Kazimirs proposal for ending APP is the most specific since ECB President Christine Lagarde signaled a tougher stance to soaring prices this month. His timing chimes with Francois Villeroy de Galhau, who said this week that purchases could finish in the third quarter. Both officials suggest a change to the ECBs forward guidance that currently calls for interest rates to rise shortly after asset purchases are concluded. Doing so would provide more optionality, according to Villeroy. lts time to start thinking about separating the two, Kazimir said. ..Phasing out asset purchases should free our hands and give us room to find the most appropriate timing for returning to rates as the standard monetary-policy tool." Other officials have urged caution in reacting to inflation that many economists still predict will come in below the ECBs 2% target in the next two years. Spains Pablo Hernandez de Cos said Thursday he sees no reason to overreact." Dropping Off Economists see euro-area inflation rates below 2% in 2023 Source: Bloomberg survey of economists, conducted Feb. 4-10 Bloomberg Chief Economist Philip Lane echoed that line later on, while also saying the ECB shouldnt tolerate under-reactions to emerging inflation risks. By contrast, other Governing Council members are keener to follow the Bank of England and the Federal Reserve in raising rates. They include Germanys Joachim Nagel and the Netherlands1 Klaas Knot, whove floated the idea of a hike as soon as this year. Investors are betting on two quarter-point increases by the end of 2022, though Latvias Martins Kazaks said this week in an interview that such a scenario is somewhat too harsh. Liftoff is nevertheless quite likely" this year, he said. The challenge for policy makers is that inflation is being driven by factors including high energy prices and supplychain bottlenecks that have lasted longer than initially thought. While the pressure is still expected to ease, unpredictable events like the tensions between Russia and the West over Ukraine are muddying the outlook. Our road-map toward monetary tightening still has some blank points that represent risks, and well need more data that will decide whether or not a rate increase will be needed already this year,11 Kazimir said. l have no doubts that were headed toward monetary tightening, but Id advocate for a path of gradual steps.11

Title: ECB should keep 50 bps hike on table, possibly for Sept: Kazimir
text: ECB should keep 50 bps hike on table, possibly for Sept: Kazimir 31. maj 2022 By Balazs Koranyi - Reuters MIKULOV, Czech Republic, May 31 (Reuters) - Record-high euro zone inflation requires the European Central Bank to raise interest rates in July and bigger moves than so far signalled may be needed to contain prices, ECB policymaker Peter Kazimir said on Tuesday. Inflation hit 8.1% in May, more than four times the ECBs 2% target, with underlying prices also soaring, challenging the banks view that 25 basis point rate hikes from July will be enough to tame stubbornly high price growth. The data, in my view cement the necessity to take the first step in raising rates, Kazimir, the relatively hawkish chief of Slovakias central bank said. My baseline is for 25 basis points (in July) but Im open to talk about 50 basis points." l expect that we will go with 25 in July, then 50 basis points could be in September," Kazimir told Reuters in an interview. The ECBs deposit rate, now at minus 0.5%, has been in negative territory since 2014 and the bank has not raised rates in over a decade. The problem is that inflation is proving more stubborn than thought just a few months ago, with even underlying inflation, which filters out volatile food and fuel prices, at more than twice the ECBs target. To tame prices, the ECB will need to raise rates back to the neutral level, where it is neither stimulating nor holding back growth, but even this may not be enough, Kazimir said. The neutral rate is somewhere between 1% and 2%. For me, it is closer to 2%,11 Kazimir said. So, what is in front of us is about a 200 (basis) point journey. We could achieve it next year.11 Asked whether that would be sufficient, Kazimir said: lt seems to me now that it wont be enough.11 NOTAT TARGET UNTIL 2025 ECB President Christine Lagarde last week said that interest rates should be back at zero or somewhat above it by the end of September, before moving toward the neutral rate later on. Most policymakers have backed a 25 basis point hike in July but several, including the central bank chiefs of the Netherlands, Austria and Latvia said that a 50 basis point move should remain on the table. The ECB until recently expected inflation back at target in 2024 but Kazimir said price growth is still going to be above target then and he now hoped to get back to 2% in 2025. Such a timeline would suggest four straight years of inflation overshoots, which risked stoking inflation expectations within the broader economy. Such de-anchoring of expectations is not yet happening, Kazimir said, but there are worrisome signs in wage-setting, which suggests that high energy costs are filtering through the economy. Kazimir added that the ECB should fight unwarranted fragmentation among the debt markets of euro zone members but he opposed a general backstop or a pre-announced tool that would kick in automatically. l think we have the capacity to come up with a tailor-made tool if its needed; I dont think we need to pre-announce details," he said. Q&As Q: May inflation figures just came out and showed yet another record high. What do you make of the figures? A: Inflation is moving up as Ive expected. The data, in my view, cement the necessity to take the first step in raising rates. We will take this step in July. How big? My baseline is 25 basis points. But Im open to talk about 50 basis points. To be realistic, I expect that we will go with 25 in July, then the 50 basis points could be in September. Whats important for me is to start hiking in July. The time for waiting, lingering, is gone. Q: What would it take for you to move towards 50 basis points In July, rather than September? A: My baseline is 25. But well have new data until then. Were data-dependent and there is one more inflation figure (June inflation flash estimate). Q: Inflation is obviously broadening. Do you see second round effects? Do you think de- anchoring is happening? A: It is definitely broadening. In all items. But I dont see de-anchoring yet. Still, we have to move to prevent de-anchoring. As for second round effects, Im very concerned. When you look at developments in wage bargaining, for example, then we definitely get very concerned. Q: What is your definition of the neutral rate? A: For me it is crucial to exit the negative deposit rate as soon as possible. For me that means September at the latest. The neutral rate is somewhere between 1% and 2%. For me, it is closer to 2%. So, what is in front of us is about a 200 (basis) point journey. Q: How long do you think this 200-basis point journey should take? A: It will depend on incoming data. We could achieve it next year. Q: Given where inflation is, and how broad its becoming, do you think getting to the neutral rate in itself is going to be enough? A: Its difficult to say now. Well have to assess data, but it seems to me now that it wont be enough. Thats my reading of the situation right now. But this requires a discussion and I think it would be best for us just to be transparent about it. I think its important to show that we are not panicking and we are taking control of the situation with an approach of optionality and flexibility. Q: Obviously, growth is going to take a hit from the (Ukraine) war. How does that figure in your own calculations? A: That definitely is going to be the case. We will also see certain fragmentation. You see and will see different developments in the countries which are more hit by the war. But at the end of the day, our primary mandate is price stability. Q: Do you see a risk of a recession? A: No, definitely not in the euro zone. A short recession is possible in some countries hit more by the war, but I do not see a euro zone-wide recession. Q: If you normalize gradually, when do you think inflation can return to target? A: We dont see it at target in 2024, so hopefully in 2025. In 2024 we could be very close to target, converging from above. Q: President (Christine) Lagarde has made it clear that the ECB will fight unwarranted fragmentation. Do you agree with this? And what is your definition of unwarranted fragmentation? A: I fully agree that euro area needs an anti-fragmentation tool, and maybe not just one, but several. But this should not be designed by the ECB. I think the main responsibility resides with elected representatives to come up with solutions that will boost resilience and fill the gaps in the euro zone architecture. It is for them to complete the banking and the capital markets union or the newly needed energy union. It is not in our capacity to deal with all the issues. Q: As for the ECB, what should its role be? A: I think its clear we have tools, we are quite experienced in this respect. We will come up with the appropriate mechanism. Also dont forget that we also have the OMT (Outright Monetary Transactions) and I still believe in market discipline. I am personally against a general backstop, with automatic rules for engagement. Q: Should the ECB pre-announce a specific anti-fragmentation tool? A: I think we have the capacity to be to come up with a tailor-made tool if its needed; I dont think we need to pre-announce details. Q: When should the discussion start about ending Asset Purchase Programme (APP) reinvestments? A: APP needs to end first! Thats the decision to take next week in Amsterdam. Its clear its going to happen but its not on paper yet. Its too early to talk about the timeframe for reinvestments. The pandemic hasnt ended yet and there is also a war. So, its unclear what the environment will be in the autumn. Q: Do you think the ECB should continue providing forward guidance? A: After July, the current forward guidance will no longer be in force. Going forward, transparency and communication will play a crucial role.

Title: ECB wants to raise interest rates in July - Governor Peter Kaimr (TA3)
text: ECB wants to raise interest rates in July - Governor Peter Kazimir (TA3) June 13, 2022 Rastislav lliev, moderator: "The decision to turn off the money printers was made by European central bankers at a meeting in Amsterdam. It was also attended by the Governor of the National Bank of Slovakia, Peter Kazimir. In an exclusive interview for TA3, he will now explain why he is back after many years interest rates in the euro area. See you Mr. Kazimir, have a nice day until Amsterdam." Peter Kazimir, Governor of the National Bank of Slovakia: "Have a good day from Amsterdam." Rastislav lliev: "The European Central Bank has decided to stop pumping billions into the economy in a month and at the same time wants to raise interest rates in July for the first time in eleven years, why did you decide to do so? It's not popular." Peter Kazimir: "Well, it's definitely not popular, but at the same time it's from the point of view of today's numbers Necessary. I think we are all aware of the increasing pressure on prices, which is taking place not only in the area of energy, but also in the area of food and all the costs associated with it Housing. But in the next one, basically also in the field of services and other goods that our citizens and companies encounter. Given that the latest figures from June this year, and given our forecasts, which see average inflation in the eurozone somewhere around 7 percent, I am now talking about a figure for the eurozone - 7 percent for the whole of this year, somewhere at 3.5 next year, and in 2024 we see inflation somewhere at the level of Back around 2 percent, somewhere at the level of 2.1 percent due to our mandate, which is related to maintaining price stability, especially in the medium term, we decided to act. Of course, we are not able to react in such a way as to stop the increase in prices, which is mainly caused by the military conflict or the failure of logistical Relations. I am thinking here of the supply of goods and services, spare parts and the various shortages of these goods. We can't solve this immediately, but we can intervene In the medium term, and in my opinion, the time is ripe. This meeting in Amsterdam was historic in terms of its conclusions. We are stopping the so-called quantitative leasing, which has been with us for years. From July 1, we will stop making so-called net purchases. And yes, we are announcing an increase in the base interest rate, we assume that we will raise the base interest rate by a quarter of a percentage point in July. And we will continue to do so in September this year, which means that the next two meetings of the Governing Council in July and September will be marked by an increase in interest rates." Rastislav lliev: "Will it be enough to slow down the record price increase, don't you think?" Peter Kazimir: "It is premature to talk about that now. Of course, data is important to us, which we collect from all over Europe and try to understand the reasons and causes. We probably all understand that the key decisions are not in the hands of politicians and economists today, but a lot really depends on the geopolitical tension that we have here in the form of real war conflict to the east of our borders. There are countries that are less and there are countries that are more sensitive to these problems. It depends, of course, on the dependence of supplies energy from the Russian Federation. Even from this point. But inflation is gradually getting to the next round, mainly through wage negotiations. And there are, of course, The decisions of governments, which, quite logically and at our call, are basically trying to rehabilitate the most vulnerable groups of citizens, which means more money in the system. And all this, of course, has inflationary pressures. So, to sum up, today it is premature to talk about how far we will rise with interest rates. We certainly do not think that these will be the levels that we see, for example, in the surrounding countries of the Middle East Europe, where interest rates are somewhere between five and six percent. This is far from the so-called neutral rate for the euro area, but we are announcing quite a transparently that the cost of financing, that is, the price of money naturally for for citizens and for companies in the euro area and therefore also in Slovakia, and this is simply a real A fact to be reckoned with. This applies, of course, to housing loans, consumer loans loans, but also corporate loans, loans that are necessary to finance our economy. Of course, we try to do these things with regard to possible negatives. In our opinion, this cautious, because it really is a very cautious approach, the so-called gradual, we are talking about gradualism, we are talking about the gradual normalization of monetary policy, because perhaps everyone will admit that many years of operating in conditions of negative interest rates is a situation that is unsustainable. So from a certain point of view, also a relief, we are coming back basically to the normal zone. Sometime this year, we will get above zero with base interest rate. And where it all goes, time will see and of course We will transparently inform about everything." Rastislav lliev: "But if the European Central Bank raises interest rates by a quarter of a percent in that first step, in September, it could be Mr. Kazimir plus or minus by how much?" Peter Kazimir: "In our instrumentation, if I call it that, it is possible to go or an increase of a quarter or half a percentage point will be considered normal. But we will decide on that in September based on completely up-to-date data from September forecasts. We live in a time when everything is really changing turbulently and we don't want to tie our hands with some concrete promises. We don't want to get ahead of the situation or scare. And we are really trying, based on the best knowledge and knowledge, to take steps that will benefit the economy, but also the citizens of the eurozone." Rastislav lliev: "Central bankers also rewrote estimates today. This year, you are expecting slower economic growth and sharper price increases than you originally expected and estimated. Is it related to the war?" Peter Kazimir: "It is related, to a large extent, if we travel a little in time, then we probably remember that we have spent the last two years, 2020 and 2021, in the convulsions of several covid wines. And we have already started to enjoy a very rapid recovery after the last wave. That revival In essence, it ignited inflationary pressures, that is, an increase in prices. Because a sharp recovery meant, it heralded that people began to spend their savings, which were essentially involuntary or unintended. Those savings arose from the fact that people could not, citizens could not actually spend their money on goods and services, because they were basically limited in consumption by lockdowns and various measures. So these forced They basically started to consume consumption, and producers, suppliers and trade were basically not able to respond with sufficient supply. This is also due to deficiencies or failures in logistical ties. I talked about them at the very beginning. Did you know that We live in a global economy today, where thousands of kilometers travel thousands of kilometers to assemble a car, a washing machine and much more ordinary products or groceries. And all these problems in logistics, they cause a shortage of goods. A logical rule, when there is a shortage of something, its price rises. So this is basically behind the first inflationary pressures. And on top of that We have basically had a military conflict that means huge speculation basically with energy prices, whether it is classic oil and important projects such as gasoline, diesel or gas, or other simply energy, other very important materials. And this, of course, causes the economy to slow down and subsequently cool down domestic consumption, the depletion of resources and savings of the population. Limiting any foreign impact. That is why we are talking about a reduction in economic growth. But we are still talking about positive numbers, that is, we are not talking about any recession yet. Although a technical recession in some countries may not be ruled out closer to a military conflict. You know that even in Slovakia, we were basically talking about economic growth before the war at a level of around five or six percent, the last forecast said about numbers between two and three percent. In two weeks, we will present our the forecast of the National Bank of Slovakia, where I am afraid that we will go a little lower with the numbers again. But still with realistic scenarios, we wouldn't have to bathe somewhere in the negatives of the recession, that is, the cessation of economic growth. So this is associated with growth. Which is a paradox that even with weak growth, we have record employment and actually huge problems on the labor market in terms of labor shortages. And this is true absolutely everywhere. And you can actually see it with your own eyes, whether at the airport in Amsterdam or in tourist centers, or even in Bratislava in the city center in terms of scarcity waiters, cooks and people who work in areas that have been very affected by COVID and those people don't seem to want to go back to work in those areas. What in turn in these sectors, of course, also causes pressure to increase wages, because people are not willing to work in these fields for pre-covid salaries. So many other phenomena. Another phenomenon that we can expect this summer season is probably the enormous interest in holidays, which we are recording even at the European level. In fact, many people logically want to enjoy a little after many months of covid wines and maybe rest and air their heads. The question is whether the capacities of the services of airlines, hotels and restaurants will be sufficient. And all this, of course, will also be reflected in prices, in higher prices. This is the world we live in today, and these are simply new things that mark our lives." Rastislav lliev: "And another thing, how many of us will be able to take that summer vacation because of the record inflation allow. From Amsterdam, the Governor of the National Bank, Peter Kazimir. Thank you very much, greetings to the Netherlands. All the best." Peter Kazimir: "Thank you. Have a nice day to you too." - increase-interest-rates-by-case-it-is-inevitable

Nechceme ani predbieha situciu, ani strai. A sname sa naozaj na zklade najlepieho vedomia a poznania robi kroky, ktor bud v prospech ekonomiky, ale aj obanov eurozny. Rastislav lliev: Centrlni bankri dnes prepisovali aj odhady. V tomto roku teda potate s pomalm ekonomickm rastom a prudm zdraovanm, ne ste pvodne oakvali a odhadovali. Svis to prve s vojnou? Peter Kaimr: Svis, do vekej miery, ak troku cestujeme v ase, tak asi si pamtme, e posledn dva roky, roky 2020 a 2021 sme preili v koch niekokch covidovch vn. A u sme sa v podstate zaali tei po poslednej vlne z vemi prudkho oivenia. To oivenie v podstate zaplilo inflan tlaky, to znamen nrast cien. Pretoe prudk oivenie znamenalo, predznamenalo to, e udia zaali ma svoje spory, ktor boli v podstate nedobrovon alebo nezaman. Tie spory vznikli z toho, e udia nemohli, obania nemohli vlastne spotrebva svoje peniaze na tovary a sluby, pretoe lockdownami a rznymi opatreniami v podstate boli obmedzovan v spotrebe. Tak tieto vynten spotreby v podstate zaali spotrebva a na to vrobcovia, dodvatelia a obchod neboli schopn v podstate reagova dostatonou ponukou. A to aj kvli nedostatkom alebo poruchm v logistickch vzbch. O tch som hovoril plne na zaiatku. Viete, e ijeme dnes v globlnej ekonomike, kde posklada auto, prku aj ovea obyajnejie produkty alebo potraviny za nami putuj tiscky kilometrov. A vetky tieto problmy v logistike spsobuj nedostatok tovarov. Logick pravidlo, ke je nieoho nedostatok, tak jeho cena stpa. Take toto je v podstate za prvmi inflanmi tlakmi. A do toho oivenia nm v podstate vbehol vojensk konflikt, ktor znamen obrovsk pekulcie v podstate s cenami energi, i u je to klasick ropa a z nej dleit projekty ako je benzn, nafta alebo plyn, alebo alie proste energie, alie vemi dleit materily. No a toto samozrejme spsobuje spomaovanie ekonomiky a aj nsledne ochladzovanie domcej spotreby, vyerpvanie aj zdrojov a spor obyvatestva. Obmedzenie nejakho zahraninho dopadu. Preto hovorme o zniovan ekonomickho rastu. Stle ale hovorme o pozitvnych slach, to znamen, nehovorme zatia o iadnej recesii. I ke technick recesia sa v niektorch krajinch mono bliie ku konfliktu vojenskmu ned vyli. Viete, e aj na Slovensku sme hovorili v podstate o ekonomickom raste ete pred vojnou na rovni okolo piatich, iestich percent, posledn prognza hovorila o slach medzi dvoma a troma percentami. O dva tdne budeme prezentova nau prognzu Nrodnej banky Slovenska, kde sa obvam, e s slami pjdeme op trochu niie. Ale stle pri realistickch scenroch by sme nemuseli sa niekde kpa v negatvach recesie, to znamen zastavenia ekonomickho rastu. Take toto je spojen s rastom. o je paradox, e aj pri slabom raste mme rekordn zamestnanos a vlastne obrovsk problmy na trhu prce z pohadu nedostatku pracovnch sl. A to plat plne vade. A vidte to vlastne na vlastn oi, i u na letisku v Amsterdame alebo v turistickch centrch, alebo aj v Bratislave v centre mesta z hadiska nedostatku ankov, kuchrov a ud, ktor pracuj v oblastiach, ktor boli vemi postihnut COVID- om a t udia akoby sa nechceli vrti pracova do tchto oblast. o zase v tchto sektoroch samozrejme znamenm aj spsobuje tlak na zvyovanie miezd, pretoe za predcovidov vlastne platy udia nie s ochotn v tchto odboroch pracova. Take mnoho alch fenomnov. al fenomn, ktor meme oakva tto letn seznu, je asi enormn zujem o dovolenky, ktor zaznamenvame dokonca aj na eurpskej rovni. Mnoho ud sa vlastne logicky chce po mnohch mesiacoch covidovch vn ako keby si trochu ui a mono odpoin a vyvetra hlavu. Otzka je, i kapacity sluieb i u leteckch spolonost, hotelov a retaurcii bud stai. A to vetko sa samozrejme odzrkadl aj v cench, vo vych cench. V takomto svete dnes ijeme a to s proste nov veci, ktor poznamenvaj nae ivoty. Rastislav lliev: A alia vec, kok z ns si bud mc t letn dovolenku pre t rekordn inflciu dovoli. Z Amsterdamu guvernr Nrodnej banky Peter Kaimr. akujem vemi pekne, pozdravujeme do Holandska. Vetko dobr. Peter Kaimr: akujem. Title: Governor Peter Kaimr in the Topic of the day on the forecast of the economy, but also on the monetary policy of the ECB (TA3)
text: Governor Peter Kazimir in the Topic of the Day on the Economic Forecast and the ECB's Monetary Policy (TA3) June 24, 2022 "Live in the studio of TA3 television. Welcome to us. Peter Kazimir, Governor of the National Bank of Slovakia: "Thank you. Good evening." Peter Bielik: "And I'm glad you're smiling, because at the last press conference we They almost didn't recognize it. You were always so jovial, so relaxed, and there it really looked like predictions, Job's rumors and various other horror emotions that came out of it." Peter Kazimir: "But I am still an optimist in life and those who know me know that I like humour, but the truth is that I have respect for the topic we talked about And we will talk about it tonight as well, and I think I also have great respect for the possible consequences, especially for specific people, for specific families, perhaps with lower incomes, which are, which are and will probably be exposed in the next two years to a situation to which they were not used in the past." Peter Bielik: "So let's divide it into small pieces or change it into small pieces. Can it fundamentally influence future developments, can we also influence it ourselves, or will we simply ride on those global trends, what is simply happening in the world simply cannot be avoided, no matter what we do?" Peter Kazimir: "Quite openly, in the short term, we can't do anything fundamental about it, hey, it's It's like when you're just sledding downhill, so you have to hold on tightly and be careful. So the situation is really serious, it is also serious precisely because we cannot read it completely, there are many, many factors that enter into it. It won't be the first time I'll just name the fact that our lives are increasingly being decided by people in uniform and not politicians, economists. There are simply those completely new phenomena that we can't quite handle every day as we would imagine, we just can't find the right medicine, the COVID pandemic, logistical problems all over the world, war, seriously just streams of people, refugees. So in this short-term situation, we can't handle it much, there, there is a key role for the state in terms of helping the weakest and those who are most exposed, I would say, to such short-term shocks, and we know those groups very well, population groups very well, and it's all over Europe, hey, so we wouldn't be able to do any in this regard, No original, but then there are medium- and long-term challenges where we have more or less chances. The world is really changing if Slovakia was a very successful example of globalization, and it really was, by simply importing foreign capital and constructing a model economy, which was simply largely based on, on its openness, on dependence on foreign trade, on the export of great products as a result A combination of the good skills and abilities of our people and foreign capital, the conditions are really changing here. And if, if global, global multinational firms were looking for in the past, the cheapest possible inputs, if they ordered such a spare part from the Philippines, one from Mexico, one from Vietnam, they understood during the pandemic that it was actually a huge risk from the point of view of just-in-time deliveries, deliveries of individual components to be able to assemble the whole, if I put it this simply. And this trend is really changing, and decisions, investment decisions are starting to be closer to production capacities, where, where production is being completed, where, where research is located, and so on. And this is on the one hand opportunity for us as well, because we are close to large, large economic powers, such as Germany, for example, which has always de facto decided in our country. geopolitical space about how, how we will live and how we will have ourselves. So that, these are the things we can talk about. And of course, of course, about that, it's also about the ability to be, to be resilient, to be more resilient, better prepared for times that may not be completely trouble-free. And these are, of course, homework for both governments and non-governmental sector, and I mean the amount of debt, fiscal discipline, some kind of plan consolidation, which will have to come after months, quarters, years without budgetary rules, but it is also about the ability to use the European Structural Funds, to have the willingness and courage to finally look at, at, our education system, to admit that we need to have a normally admitted, rational, reasonable migration policy, which is not a sin, they laugh, they are able to solve very effectively under pressure, but we do not have any well-thought-out plan like other countries have, that are struggling, struggling with aging, or even with the exodus of young people from some parts of our country. So, so these are things, these are such long-term illnesses, hey, which, and weaknesses that we have. And we know the list, the ugly list very well, the other thing is whether we are willing to deal with them, whether we have the courage to do so and whether we are ready for it." Peter Bielik: "Well, it looks like a pretty decent reconstruction of the whole country, because we have really been built as a pro-export economy for those twenty or twenty-five years, basically an assembly workshop, of course, with all the added values that it has, I don't want to reduce it, but now, if globalization is now hitting some of its limits, as you said, so what, we will have to rely more on internal consumption, we will strengthen the state as it used to be, that is, we will want to be more robust in social services, Will we want to be more robust in those non-manufacturing spheres, these are the solutions you are talking about?" Peter Kazimir: "We are talking about a new business model that has to be more concentrated on added value, hey? It's like, if you just have countries that are lucky enough to have large mineral resources, so often this treasure actually spoils their future by not being able to give added value, because they simply sell the raw material expensively, and that, in fact, simply spoils their future. Of course, this does not apply to all such countries, but it is very important to think there, to think about the future. So, so In our case, and I don't like the term assembly workshop, it is something that is just a bit humiliating, but we are a highly sophisticated, specialized assembly workshop, not an assembly workshop, but it deals with a very sophisticated type of engineering and simply an area of industry that is very complex in its essence. You know, if we have four major factories here, car manufacturers, maybe there will be another one in a while, but the key thing is another three hundred and fifty - four hundred small, medium, larger suppliers of spare parts, but they export all over the world, not just to these four suppliers. So I know all the theoretical reservations about the fact that we are too dependent on the automotive industry, it is logically, academically simply a true statement, but in fact, the automotive industry has so far pulled us out of every mess we have been in, and whether it was the crisis in 2009, and that was some kind of crisis, or another one and other minor crises, which, unfortunately, are very, very often just starting to come in certain waves. So this type of industry, this type of industry just for the time being He did not disappoint, but it is true and it must be said that it is getting worse and worse for our investors to look for the most precious thing, and that is the workforce, hey? We don't have enough people, every employer in Slovakia will tell you that, whether they speak Slovak or not, everyone will tell you that the biggest problem is the people, hey, so. And it's not that we have a bad mentality, we, we just don't have enough qualified people. And that is, of course, connected to the system, to our education system, to our, with the exodus of our young people abroad, hey, which is to some extent just A natural phenomenon, young people want to travel, they want to get to know new cultures, but they have, they should also have the effort to just come back at some point. So this is just A comprehensive approach to the most important factor of production, the factor of production, the factor that is people, right?" Peter Bielik: "And what should this new business model of Slovakia be?" Peter Kazimir: "The business model should be based on the ability to add more added value. And that is, it's just sophisticated production, it's, it's just research and it is a certain degree of diversification in other areas, these are different innovations, that we talk about endlessly. Whether it's financial services or innovations in industry, it doesn't matter from this point of view, it's just that progress is important, in any case, in every case." Peter Bielik: "So to take it further, what we have at the moment, not to change it from the ground up, but to get it to a higher level." Peter Kazimir: "Life is impossible, the conditions cannot be changed like this, it is not possible. As it is important for us, of course, to have the most acceptable business environment, a calculable political scene, a certain kind of stability simply is, is, is necessary." Peter Bielik: "So everything we don't have, OK." Peter Kazimir: "That's all that we may have had in part and in part, sometimes it just comes, sometimes it leaves. It's just a thing that maybe we have to deserve." Peter Bielik: "As far as the automotive industry is concerned, there will have to be a big fight between electricity and hydrogen. We know how it is at the moment in terms of the political setting, Richard Sulik is a fan of hydrogen, the automotive industry does not even want to hear about it yet, so we will see. Let's take a look at what bothers you the most, and that is the development of inflation. So what does the current forecast look like in terms of the amount of inflation and the length of that inflation, how long can it last?" Peter Kazimir: "Well, if we were talking about height, then if I used a sporty, sporting expression, then two elevens would shine on the scoreboard, eleven eleven. And these are, unfortunately, simply our estimates of how we see average inflation for 2022, for this year, and what inflation could look like next year. That is, these are two-digit numbers, this is something that we simply did not know here. As some of us may remember, and when you We remember, it didn't bother us so much in the nineties, we were both probably young, much younger, and it probably didn't bother us that much when the inflation numbers were short period higher, but the truth is that between 2009 and 2020, the average inflation is somewhere only around one percent. And it wasn't until last year that it started to climb somewhere to four - Four and a half percent, hey, I would say, people raised their eyebrows that what a new phenomenon this is, that something is more expensive, because some have never experienced it and some last experienced it fifteen or twenty years ago. And the development that is coming for the next two years, and we live in the middle of it, is, it talks about double-digit numbers, so ten, eleven, it's worse every month. We really make four official forecasts a year and twelve unofficial forecasts for, for ourselves, and every month our forecasts are basically old and the situation is getting worse because, of course, the numbers are then reported by the Statistical Office and they are simply surprises. And it's not just surprises in our country, as numbers, in Estonia there is twenty percent inflation, just a crazy number, hey, in Germany, with which we have so much in terms of the economy, it's, it's a number somewhere around just eight percent." Peter Bielik: "And they are afraid of a recession, in the big economy, in Germany." Peter Kazimir: "We can all be afraid of a recession, it is simply a scenario that can realistically occur, but rather in the form of a technical recession, which in our opinion could last for a very short time, but such a development is very, very much connected with the topic that you have dealt with here in the previous forty minutes. And I don't know, you found out About when the war will end?" Peter Bielik: "No." Peter Kazimir: "Because, because this is simply an absolute basic question that neither you nor we can answer, probably not even our leaders at the summit that is currently taking place can answer it. And yes, if, if the conflict worsens, here it is already We are not even talking about a frozen conflict, if it were to be aggravated, for example, by a really sudden disruption of the supply of essential energy carriers, such as gas or In some later period of nuclear fuel, so, so, then we're going to face a really serious possible economic downturn, and we're talking about a few, just a recession In a few percent, hey, these are just estimates. Of course, then she would have to The topic of solidarity of the European Union should be raised, because simply in the European Union, in the Union, there are countries that are really very differently exposed to this situation. Believe me, in Iberian On the peninsula, people simply do not address this topic over coffee or evening beer, they do not perceive it, it is too far away for them, as far away as those thousands of refugees from the North Africa, which landed every day in rubber boats on the Spanish coasts, hey, that was also something for us, just that was not tangible and within reach, but the war, the war in Ukraine and the conflict east of our borders in general is, has a very real impact simply on how we are perceived as a country. This has an impact even on the risk premiums on our bonds, because we belong together with the Baltic countries and with other countries bordering Ukraine, geographically, quite logically, for investors who sit in the City of London, we are one of the riskier and more risky countries automatically. So, so these are just new phenomena that we just have to get used to, and from a certain point of view, we will have to pay for them." Peter Bielik: "Now I'll ask you maybe more as a former finance minister. Igor Matovi admits that he has a loaded credit card, so to speak. He borrowed to Vseobecna Treasury administration, that cheap money, when it was still cheap, even with negative interest rates and so on, in the range, and I don't know now, we don't know exactly the number, between seven and ten billion. The last time he sat here, he told me that he had a hard time repayment of our debt. The question is, why doesn't he repay the debt faster, when we have this cheap money borrowed and at the moment it is probably difficult to predict that the money They will be cheaper, or that we will borrow something else, more advantageously, simply these are, this is the maximum possible that we have probably been able to get in terms of cheap money. And as far as I know, one percent of GDP, if we are talking about it, is about one billion. Now that we have seven to ten billion deposited somewhere, wouldn't we be able to use them more efficiently than lying around somewhere?" Peter Kazimir: "Like this. First of all, maybe I'm being too conservative, but, but it's not appropriate to talk about how much money the state has, I'm telling you really deadly seriously, whether it has a lot or a little, it's just information that is available to the people who are supposed to have it." Peter Bielik: "So the current Minister of Finance took it differently and said this information." Peter Kazimir: "It's completely, like this, it's public, it's public information, what is the country's emission plan, hey? This means that we borrow somewhere around seven or eight a year billions a year as standard, and there is a very clear plan when we have maturing bonds, debts from the past. And in fact, the absolute majority of our bond issues are used to repay old debts, so the debt is constantly rolling. Then another reason for the issue is, of course, the deficit. This means that if a country runs a deficit, which our country has always managed in its modern history so far, then you need to cover it again by issuing government bonds. So the issuance plan actually consists of a plan, and it is quite clear, a debt that needs to be paid and a new debt that arises. Of course, there are situations, and there have been in the past, when it is reasonable to stock up. This is perhaps also a topic that you have caught in connection with the Budget Responsibility Act, that is net versus gross debt. So there, that's too technical a debate for this evening's hour, but the truth is that sometimes, and this is a matter that is completely understandable even to the common sense, that there may be periods when it is reasonable, especially in periods of great uncertainty to have, to sit on money, if I were to put it that way, completely on the shovel. And I think that happened in 2020, because it was a shocking year of the onset of the pandemic, when the markets really closed again for a while, and those who had money and supplies had, who didn't, so they just turned green maybe or had some other problems, but that didn't happen to our country either, someone didn't turn green here, no one dropped out, everyone got paid, The country simply fulfilled its obligations, but it is also true that it was simply profitable to continue borrowing. So, if there is a reserve today, and I don't have these numbers, so, so, then it is primarily intended for the two purposes that I mentioned, to pay off old debts, and there is a clear calendar that you can't get very ahead of, that, I would say, early repayment, those thousands of small creditors who are behind the big ones would have to agree to that companies that trade on the international financial market, so, and the second option is, the matter is how the deficit will end, and the Ministry of Finance always knows the most about this. All the rest of us are just thinking about it, but the truth is that The Minister of Finance and his people know the most about it, hey, and that's absolutely right and that's how it should be." Peter Bielik: "Okay, so we're sitting on money, wouldn't you see any better use for it?" Peter Kazimir: "So, you know, that's money that can only be used by legal way, hey, that is, there are clear rules, what is not in the state budget, that's right, it's hard to just pay for some additional emissions. You even have to tell your creditors in advance for what purpose you are using the money. So, from that point of view, it can't be used for any other purpose than I've just named. And that, the rest is just really micromathematics about the fact that whether in times when there is very little interest on deposits, someone could compare whether we lose on it or something, we earn something, but it must be said that behind the work with money there are really great experts whom I personally had the honor to know." Peter Bielik: "Okay, so you don't see this as a problem again." Peter Kazimir: "I'm talking about ARDAL, the Debt and Liquidity Management Agency, and I'm talking about the State Treasury. And these are simply teams of people who know very well what they are doing." Peter Bielik: "In short, Mr. Governor, if you will allow me, how should the European Central Bank react at the moment in terms of interest rates? It is already being fully said that it will be now during the summer, that it will not be at the end of the year, as originally stated It was assumed, there would be an increase in interest rates. Where would you see such an interest rate that could at least slightly suppress inflation downwards?" Peter Kazimir: "There is a lot of mystery around central banking and decisions in central banking, but this is really not a secret, what you have named. Yes, at the meeting two weeks ago in Amsterdam, the Governing Council decided that, on the one hand, it is stopping the asset purchase programme after many years, that the so-called quantitative easing is simply stopping, and this will happen from the first of July, and on the other hand, we are, in fact, announcing, which is a relatively progressive procedure, we are announcing that in July, at the July meeting, it will be sometime at the end of July, For the first time in many, many, many years, we will raise rates, and it will most likely be by twenty-five percentage points, which means by a quarter of a percent. And we assume that In September, we will decide to raise rates again, and this time by half a percent. That is what we are publicly proclaiming today on the basis of the data we had on the date negotiations in Amsterdam, based on the latest May inflation figures in the euro area. Of course, it will be important for us, after months, how it develops, what the numbers for June will be, and that will be key for the decision in July, and then what will happen during the holidays. So we will, since we say that we are, We decide for, based on real information and real numbers, so the trend is clear, hey, that is, we are going, we are turning as if from easing to tightening, even though We say it, we talk about normalization. In the first step, we want to finally get into the realm of real numbers, that is, plus a week, hey, because we have actually had negative base rates for years. And if you were to ask me where it could end, the way we see it today, well, sometimes, if the situation did not deteriorate fundamentally, then sometime in a year we could be somewhere about two percent higher than it is today, that is, somewhere between one and a half and two percent of the rate, Talking on base rates. Of course, the financial markets are already reacting, the banks." Peter Bielik: "What we are, we really haven't had for years." Peter Kazimir: "We haven't had that for years, but we really just need to prepare for that. And if Ours, if our estimates in a year's time are such that we still see it badly, because we are simply looking at the period of a year and a half and two years ahead, ahead of us, so now we are actually targeting the level of inflation in 2004, and if next year we will continue to see inflation in 2005 beyond our goal, we will basically have to continue." Peter Bielik: "2025." Peter Kazimir: "We will have to continue raising rates further." Peter Bielik: "Mr. Governor, then, of course, there will be such micro-counting, when it is reflected in mortgages, when it is reflected in loans." Peter Kazimir: "This is already happening today." Peter Bielik: "That will be, it will be a good opportunity to discuss it in more detail." Peter Kazimir: "This is already happening today, and of course, banks and all those who simply work with money are reacting to this. We have had several months of enormous pressure on refixations, which means that banks gave clients the opportunity, just as Minister Sulik actually came up with the idea of a possible fixation or the expected development of gas prices for, for households, when agreeing on what it will look like in the next four years For years, similarly, banks gave people the opportunity to actually fix the interest rate for a fee." Peter Bielik: "I thought that when the increase in those interest rates, the recalculation will then be fully manifested, although of course, financial institutions are already intensively preparing for this. The European Central Bank does not hide this intention at all. Thank you very much, Mr. Governor, for taking the time for our viewers tonight." Peter Kazimir: "Thank you for the invitation. Have a beautiful evening to you too." Peter Bielik: "Have a nice evening."
text_original: Guvernr Peter Kaimr v Tme da o prognze vvoja ekonomiky, ale aj menovej politike ECB (TA3) 24. jn 2022 Naivo v tdiu televzie TA3. Vitajte u ns. Peter Kaimr, guvernr Nrodnej banky Slovenska: akujem. Dobr veer. Peter Bielik: A som rd, e sa usmievate, lebo na tej poslednej tlaovke sme vs takmer nespoznvali. Vy ste boli vdy tak ovilny, tak uvonenej, a tam to vyzeralo ako naozaj predpovede, Jbove zvesti a rzne in hororov emcie, ktor z toho ili. Peter Kaimr: Ja som ale stle ivotn optimista a t, ktor ma poznaj, vedia, e mm rd humor, aleje pravdou, e, e mm repekt voi tej tme, o ktorej sme hovorili a budeme o nej aj dnes veer hovori, a mm, myslm si, e aj vek repekt k monm nsledkom hlavne na konkrtnych ud, na konkrtne rodiny mono s nimi prjmami, ktor, ktor s, ktor s a bud zrejme v najblich dvoch rokoch vystaven situcii, na ktor neboli v minulosti zvyknut. Peter Bielik: Tak pome si to rozdeli na drobn alebo rozmeni na drobn. Me budci vvoj zsadne ovplyvni, meme ho ovplyvni aj my sami alebo sa jednoducho u len zvezieme na tch globlnych trendoch, to, o sa deje jednoducho vo svete, sa nm jednoducho nevyhne, nech robme, o robme? Peter Kaimr: plne otvorene, krtkodobo s tm nevieme ni zsadn urobi, hej, je to, ako ke proste sa snkujete z kopca, take sa treba poriadne dra a treba si dva pozor. Take t situcia je naozaj vna, je vna aj prve preto, e ju nevieme plne ta, vstupuje do nich, do nej proste vea, vea faktorov. Nebude to prv raz, ke proste pomenujem to, e o naich ivotoch oraz viac rozhoduj udia v uniformch a nie politici, ekonmovia. Proste s tu tie plne nov javy, s ktormi nevieme plne narba kad de tak, ako by sme si predstavovali, nevieme proste njs t, t sprvnu medicnu, COVID pandmia, logistick problmy krom-krom po svete, vojna, vne proste prdy ud, uteenci. Take v tejto situcii krtkodobo to vea nevieme zvldnu, tam, tam je kov loha naozaj ttu z pohadu toho, aby pomohol tm najslabm a tm, ktor s najviac vystaven, by som povedal, takm krtkodobm okom, a tie skupiny vemi dobre, skupiny obyvatestva vemi dobre poznme a je to krom-krom po celej Eurpe, hej, ie v tomto pohade by sme neboli iadny, iadny originl, ale potom s tu strednodob a dlhodob vzvy, kde mme vie alebo menie ance. Svet sa naozaj men, ak Slovensko bolo vemi spenm prkladom globalizcie, a to naozaj bolo, dovozom proste zahraninho kapitlu a skontruovanm modelu ekonomiky, ktor bol proste do vekej miery zaloen na, na svojej otvorenosti, na zvislosti na zahraninom obchode, na vvoze skvelch vrobkov ako vsledku kombincie dobrho umu a schopnosti naich ud a zahraninho kapitlu, tak tu sa naozaj menia podmienky. A ak, ak globlna, globlne nadnrodn firmy hadali v minulosti o najlacnejie vstupy, ak si objednvali tak nhradn diel z Filipn, tak z Mexika, tak z Vietnamu, tak pochopili v ase pandmie, e je to vlastne obrovsk riziko z pohadu just in time dodvok, dodvok jednotlivch siastok na to, aby sme mohli zmontova celok, ak to poviem takto jednoducho. A tento trend sa naozaj men a rozhodnutia, investin rozhodnutia zanaj by bliie k vrobnm kapacitm, kde sa, kde sa finiuje vroba, kde, kde je vskum a podobne. A toto je na jednej strane prleitos aj, aj pre ns, pretoe sme blzko vekch, vekch mocnost ekonomickch, ako je, ako je Nemecko naprklad, ktor vdycky de facto rozhodovalo v naom geopolitickom priestore o tom, ako, ako budeme i a ako sa budeme ma. Take to, to s veci, o ktorch vieme hovori. A samozrejme, samozrejme, o tom, je to aj o schopnosti by, by rezistentn, by odolnej, lepie pripraven na asy, ktor nemusia by plne bezproblmov. A to s, samozrejme, domce lohy aj, pre vldy, aj pre mimovldny sektor a mm na mysli vku dlhu, fiklnu disciplnu, nejak pln konsolidcie, ktor bude musie prs po mesiacoch, tvrrokoch, rokoch bez rozpotovch pravidiel, ale je to aj o schopnosti vyuva eurpske trukturlne fondy, ma ochotu a odvahu pozrie sa konene na, na, na n vzdelvac systm, prizna si, e potrebujeme ma normlne priznan, racionlnu, rozumn migran politiku, ktor nie je hriechom, smej, smej schopn pod tlakom proste vemi efektvne riei, ale nemme iadny premyslen pln, ako maj in krajiny, ktor bojuj, bojuj s starnutm, alebo dokonca s exodusom mladch ud z niektorch ast naej krajiny. Take, take to s veci, to s tak dlhodob choroby, hej, ktor, a slabosti, ktor, ktor mme. A my ten zoznam, ten kared zoznam vemi dobre poznme, druh vec je, i sme ich ochotn riei, i na to mme odvahu a i sme na to pripraven. Peter Bielik: No, tak to vyzer na celkom slun prestavbu celho ttu, pretoe naozaj sme boli tch dvadsa - dvadsap rokov budovan ako proexportn ekonomika, v podstate montna diela, samozrejme, s vetkmi tmi pridanmi hodnotami, o to m, ja to nechcem zniova, ale teraz, ak teraz nara globalizcia, ako ste povedali, na nejak svoje limity, tak o, budeme sa musie spoahn viac na vntorn spotrebu, budeme posilova tt, ako to bolo kedysi, to znamen budeme chcie by robustnej v socilnych slubch, budeme chcie by robustnej v tch nevrobnch sfrach, toto s tie rieenia, o ktorch hovorte? Peter Kaimr: Hovorme o novom biznismodeli, ktor viac mus by koncentrovan na pridan hodnotu, hej? To je ako, ak mte proste krajiny, ktor, ktor maj to astie, e maj vek nerastn suroviny, tak asto ich, tento poklad skaz im vlastne budcnos tm, e, e nie s schopn da pridan hodnotu, lebo proste draho predaj surovinu, a to ich, vlastne, im proste pokaz ich budcnos. Netka sa to, samozrejme, vetkch takchto krajn, ale tam je vemi dleit myslie, myslie na budcnos. Take, take v naom prpade, a ja nemm rd vraz montna diela, je to nieo, o je tak proste ako keby trochu poniujce, ale my sme vysoko sofistikovan, pecializovan montna, nie montna diela, ktor sa ale venuje vemi sofistikovanmu typu strojrenstva a proste oblasti priemyslu, ktor je vemi komplexn vo svojej, vo svojej podstate. Viete, ak tu mme tyri vznamn fabriky, automobilky, mono o chvu bude alia, tak ale to kov je alch tristopdesiat - tyristo malch, strednch, vch dodvateov nhradnch dielov, ktor ale exportuj do celho sveta, nielen tmto tyrom dodvateom. Take ja poznm vetky tie teoretick vhrady o tom, e sme prli zvisl na automobilovom priemysle, ono to logicky, akademicky je proste pravdiv vrok, ale v skutonosti ns automobilov priemysel zatia vytiahol z kadej lamastiky, v ktorej sme boli, a i to u bola krza v roku 2009, a to bola teda nejak krza, alebo alie a alie menie krzy, ktor, bohuia, vemi, vemi asto zanaj proste prichdza v istch vlnch. Take ns tento typ industry, tento typ priemyslu proste zatia nesklamal, aleje pravdou a treba si poveda, e je oraz horie pre naich investorov hada to najvzcnejie, a to je pracovn sila, hej? My nemme dostatok ud, to vm povie kad zamestnvate na Slovensku, i hovor alebo nehovor po slovensky, kad vm povie, e najv problm s udia, hej, take. A to nie je o tom, e by sme mali zl mentalitu, my, my nemme proste dostatok kvalifikovanch ud. A to je, samozrejme, spojen so systmom, s naim vzdelvacm systmom, s naim, s exodusom naich mladch ud do zahraniia, hej, ktor je z istej asti proste prirodzenm javom, mlad udia chc cestova, chc poznva nov kultry, ale maj, mali by ma aj snahu v nejakom ase sa potom proste vraca. Take toto je proste komplexn prstup k najdleitejiemu vrobnho faktoru, vrobnmu faktoru, faktoru, ktorm s udia, no? Peter Bielik: A v om by mal by tento nov obchodn model teda Slovenska? Peter Kaimr: Ten obchodn model kovo m by zaloen na schopnosti pridva viu pridan hodnotu. A tou je, je proste sofistikovan vroba, je to, proste je to vskum a je to ist miera diverzifikcie v alch oblastiach, s to rzne inovcie, o ktorch donekonena hovorme. i s to finann sluby alebo inovcie v priemysle, to je plne jedno z tohto pohadu, proste dleit je progres, v kadom, v kadom prpade. Peter Bielik: Take potiahnu to alej, to, o mme v sasnosti, nie to od zkladu meni, ale dosta to na vyiu rove. Peter Kaimr: ivot sa ned, tie podmienky sa nedaj akoe takto proste zmeni, to nie je mon. Akoe pre ns je dleit ma, samozrejme, o najprijatenejie podnikatesk prostredie, vypotaten politick scnu, ist druh stability proste je, je, je nevyhnutn. Peter Bielik: Take vetko to, o nemme v podstate, OK. Peter Kaimr: To je vetko to, o sme mono niekedy sasti mali a sasti, raz to proste prichdza, raz to odchdza. Je to proste vec, ktor si mono aj musme zasli. Peter Bielik: o sa tka automobilovho priemyslu, tam sa bude musie zvies vek boj medzi elektrinou a vodkom. Vieme, ako to v sasnosti je z hadiska politickho nastavenia, Richard Sulk fand vodku, automobilov priemysel o tom nechce zatia ani pou, tak uvidme. Pome sa pozrie na to, o trpi vs najviac, a to je vvoj inflcie. Ako vyzer teda t aktulna prognza z hadiska vky inflcie a z hadiska dky tej inflcie, ako dlho to me trva? Peter Kaimr: No, keby sme hovorili o vke, tak keby som pouil portov, portov vraz, tak na vsledkovej tabuli by svietili dve jedenstky, jedens jedens. A to s, bohuia, proste nae odhady, ako vidme priemern inflciu za rok 2022, za tento rok, a ako by mohla vyzera inflcia v budcom roku. To znamen, to s dvojcifern sla, to je nieo, o sme tu proste nepoznali. Ako mono si niektor pamtme, a ke si to pamtme, tak ns to a tak netrpilo v devdesiatych rokoch, to sme boli obaja asi mlad, ovea mlad a asi ns to a tak netrpilo, ke tie inflan sla boli krtke obdobie vyie, ale pravdou je, e medzi rokmi 2009 a 2020 je t priemern inflcia niekde iba okolo jednho percenta. A a minul rok sa to zaalo plha niekde k tyrom - tyri a pol percentm, hej to u tak, by som povedal, zdvihli udia oboie, e o to je za nov fenomn, e nieo je drahie, pretoe niektor to nikdy nezaili a niektor to zaili naposledy pred ptnstimi - dvadsiatimi rokmi. No a ten vvoj, ktor prichdza na najbliie dva roky, a ijeme uprostred neho, je, hovor o dvojcifernch slach, ie desa, jedens, kad mesiac je to horie. My naozaj robme tyri oficilne prognzy do roka a dvans neoficilnych pre, pre seba a kad mesiac s proste nae prognzy v podstate star a t situcia sa zhoruje, pretoe, samozrejme, sla dona potom tatistick rad a s to proste prekvapenia. A nie s to prekvapenia len u ns, ako sla, v Estnsku je dvadsapercentn inflcia, proste ialen slo, hej, v Nemecku, s ktorm mme tak strane vea z hadiska, z hadiska ekonomiky, je to, je to slo niekde okolo proste smich percent. Peter Bielik: A obvaj sa recesie, vo vekej ekonomike, v Nemecku. Peter Kaimr: Vetci sa meme obva aj recesie, to je proste scenr, ktor, ktor me relne nasta, ale skr v takej, zatia skr v takej podobe technickej recesie, ktor by mohla trva poda ns vemi krtko, ale takto vvoj je vemi, vemi spojen s tmou, ktor ste tu rieili tch predchdzajcich tyridsa mint. A neviem, dozvedeli ste sa o tom, kedy skon vojna? Peter Bielik: No. Peter Kaimr: Lebo, lebo to je proste absoltna zkladn otzka, na ktor ani vy, ani, ani my nevieme odpoveda, nevedia na u odpoveda zrejme ani nai ldri na summite, ktor prve aktulne proste prebieha. A no, keby, keby sa konflikt zhoril, tu u nehovorme ani o zamrznutom konflikte, ak by sa zhoril naprklad naozaj nhlym preruenm dodvok zkladnch energetickch nosiov, naprklad plynu alebo v nejakom neskorom obdob jadrovho paliva, tak, tak, tak potom budeme eli naozaj vnemu monmu ekonomickmu prepadu a hovorme o niekoko, proste o recesii v niekokch percentch, hej, to s proste odhady. Samozrejme, vtedy by musela nastpi tma solidarity Eurpskej nie, pretoe proste v Eurpskej nie, nii s krajiny, ktor s naozaj vemi rzne vystaven tejto, tejto situcii. Verte mi, e na Iberijskom polostrove proste tto tmu udia pri kve alebo pri veernom pive nerieia, nevnmaj, je to pre nich prli aleko, rovnako aleko, ako pre ns boli tie tisce uteencov zo severnej Afriky, ktor, ktor kad de pristvali v gumench lnoch na, na panielskych pobreiach, hej, to bolo pre ns tie nieo, proste o nebolo hmataten a na dosah, ale vojna, vojna na Ukrajine a vbec konflikt na vchod od naich hranc je, m vemi relny dosah proste na to, ako sme aj my vnman ako krajina. To m dopad dokonca aj na rizikov prirky na nae dlhopisy, pretoe my patrme spolu s baltskmi krajinami a s almi krajinami, ktor hraniia s Ukrajinou, geograficky, plne logicky, pre investorov, ktor sedia v londnskej City, patrme medzi rizikov a viac rizikov krajiny automaticky tm pdom. Take, take to s proste nov fenomny, na ktor si musme proste zvykn, a z istho pohadu za ne budeme musie aj zaplati. Peter Bielik: Teraz sa vs optam mono ako bvalho ministra financi viac. Igor Matovi priznva, e m takpovediac nabit kreditku. On si poial do Veobecnej pokladninej sprvy tie lacn peniaze, ke ete teda boli lacn, dokonca so zpornmi rokmi a tak alej, v rozmedz, a teraz neviem, nepoznme plne presne to slo, medzi siedmimi a desiatimi miliardami. Naposledy, ke tu sedel, mi tvrdil, e to m na splcanie nho dlhu. Otzkou je, preo teda ten dlh nesplca rchlejie, ke mme tieto lacn peniaze poian a v sasnosti je asi ako predpoveda, e tie peniaze bud lacnejie, alebo e si poiiame ete inak, vhodnejie, jednoducho toto s, to je to maximum monho zrejme, o sme z hadiska lacnch peaz dokzali zska. A pokia viem, tak jedno percento HDP, ak teda o om hovorme, je zhruba jedna miliarda. Ke mme teraz sedem a desa milird niekde odloench, nevedeli by sme ich poui efektvnejie, ako e nm niekde leia? Peter Kaimr: Takto. Po prv, mono som prli konzervatvny, ale, ale neslu sa plne hovori o tom, koko m tt peaz, to vm hovorm naozaj smrtene vne, i ich m vea alebo mlo, to s proste informcie, s ktormi disponuj udia, ktor nimi maj disponova. Peter Bielik: Tak pn minister financi sasn to vzal inak a tto informciu povedal. Peter Kaimr: Je plne, takto, je verejn, je verejnou informciou, ak je emisn pln krajiny, hej? To znamen, my si rone poiiavame niekde okolo siedmich - smich milird rone plne tandardne a je plne jasn pln, kedy mme splatn dlhopisy, dlhy z minulosti. A v podstate absoltna vina tch emisi naich dlhopisov je pouit prve na splcanie starch dlhov, ie ten dlh sa neustle roluje. Potom alm dvodom emisie je, samozrejme, deficit. To znamen, ak krajina hospodri deficitn, o naa krajina hospodrila vdy v svojej modernej histrii zatia, tak, tak to potrebujete vykry op emisiou ttnych dlhopisov. Take ten emisn pln sa sklad vlastne z plnu a ten je plne jasn, dlhu, ktor treba zaplati, a novho dlhu, ktor, ktor vznik. Samozrejme, s situcie a boli aj v minulosti, ke je rozumn sa predzsobi. To je mono aj tma, ktor ste zachytili v svislosti so zkonom o rozpotovej zodpovednosti, to je ist verzus hrub dlh. Take tam, to je prli technick debata na tto veern hodinu, ale pravdou je, e niekedy, a to je plne aj sedliackym rozumom pochopiten zleitos, e, e mu by obdobia, ke je rozumn, hlavne v obdobiach vekej neistoty ma, sedie na peniazoch, ak by som to takto povedal, plne po lopate. A myslm, e to sa udialo v roku 2020, pretoe to bol okov rok nstupu pandmie, ke sa naozaj na chvu op trhy zavreli, a kto mal peniaze a zsoby, mal, kto nemal, tak proste ozelenel mono alebo mal nejak in problmy, ale to sa naej krajine tie akoe nestalo, niekto tu neozelenel, nikto neodpadol, kad dostal vplatu, krajina si proste dostla svojich zvzkov, aleje aj pravdou, e, e bolo proste vhodn si alej poiiava. Take, ak dneska nejak rezerva je, a ja nedisponujem tmito slami, tak, tak, tak je primrne uren na tie dva ely, ktor som spomnal, na splatenie starch dlhov a tam je jasn kalendr, ktor neviete vemi predbehn, to, to by som, predasn splcanie, s tm by museli shlasi tie tiscky drobnch veriteov, ktor, ktor s za tmi vekmi spolonosami, ktor, ktor obchoduj na trhu medzinrodnom finannom, take, a druh monos je, zleitos je, ako skon deficit, a o tom vdycky najviac vie ministerstvo financi. To vetci ostatn okolo toho len mudrujeme, ale pravdou je, e najviac o tom vie minister financi a jeho udia, hej, a to je plne sprvne a tak to m aj by. Peter Bielik: Dobre, take sedme na peniazoch, nevideli by ste pre ne nejak lepie vyuitie? Peter Kaimr: Tak, viete, to, to s peniaze, ktor sa daj poui iba zkonnm spsobom, hej, to znamen, s jasn povedan pravidl, to, o nie je v ttnom rozpote, tak je, je ako z nejakch dodatonch emisi proste nejako plati. Vy muste dokonca svojim veriteom dopredu oznmi, akm, na ak el tie peniaze pouvate. Take, z tohto pohadu to, to nie je mon poui na in el, ako som, ako som proste pomenoval. A to, zvyok je u proste naozaj mikromatematika o tom, e i v asoch, ke s vemi mal roky na lokch, niekto by mohol porovna teda, i na tom strcame alebo nieo, nieo zarbame, ale treba poveda, e za, za prcou s peniazmi s naozaj skvel odbornci, ktorch osobne som mal t es pozna. Peter Bielik: Dobre, take zase toto ako problm nevidte. Peter Kaimr: Hovorm o ARDAL, o Agentre pre riadenie dlhu a likvidity a hovorm o ttnej pokladnici. A to s proste tmy ud, ktor vemi dobre vedia, o robia. Peter Bielik: Kratuko, pn guvernr, ak dovolte, ako by mala Eurpska centrlna banka momentlne reagova, o sa tka rokovch sadzieb? U sa naplno hovor, e to bude teraz poas leta, e to nebude teda a na konci roka, ako pvodne sa predpokladalo, prde k zveniu rokovch sadzieb. Kde by ste videli vy tak t rokov sadzbu, ktor by dokzala aspo troku potlai t inflciu smerom dole? Peter Kaimr: Okolo centrlneho bankrstva a rozhodnut v centrlnom bankovnctve je vea tajomstva, ale toto naozaj tajomstvo nie je, to, o ste pomenovali. no, na zasadnut pred dvoma tdami v Amsterdame rada guvernrov rozhodla o tom, e jednak zastavuje program na kpu aktv po mnohch rokoch, proste prestva takzvan kvantitatvne uvoovanie, a tak sa udeje od prvho jla, a jednak sme, vlastne avizujeme, o je relatvne progresvny postup, avizujeme, e v jli, na jlovom zasadnut, to bude niekedy koncom jla, prvkrt po mnohch, mnohch, mnohch rokoch zdvihneme sadzby a vysoko pravdepodobne to bude o dvadsap percent bzickch bodov, o znamen o tvr percenta udskou reou. A predpokladme, e v septembri rozhodneme op o zdvihnut sadzieb a tento krt o pol percenta. To je to, k omu sa dneska verejne hlsime na zklade dajov, ktor sme mali k dtumu rokovania v Amsterdame, ie na zklade poslednch mjovch sel o inflcii v eurozne. Bude pre ns, samozrejme, dleit, po mesiacoch ako sa to bude vyvja, ak bud sla za jn, a to bude kov pre rozhodnutie v jli, a potom nsledne o bude cez przdniny. Take my sa budeme, kee hovorme, e sme, sa rozhodujeme za, na zklade relnych informci a relnych sel, tak ten trend je jasn, hej, to znamen, ideme, otame ako keby od uvoovania k sprsovaniu, aj ke hovorme to, hovorme o normalizcii. V prvom kroku sa chceme dosta konene do, do sfry relnych sel, to znamen plusovch tde, hej, lebo sme, sme roky mali vlastne negatvne zkladn sadzby. No a ak by ste ma optali, kde by to mohlo skoni, tak tak, ako to vidme dnes, tak, tak niekedy, ak by sa situcia zsadnm spsobom nezhorila, tak by sme niekedy o rok mohli by niekde asi o dve percent vyie, ako je to dnes, to znamen niekde medzi okolo jeden a pol a dvoch percent sadzby, hovorme o zkladnch sadzbch. Samozrejme, finann trhy u reaguj, banky. Peter Bielik: o sme, to sme naozaj roky nemali. Peter Kaimr: To sme roky nemali, ale na to sa treba relne proste pripravi. A ak nae, ak nae odhady o rok bud tak, e to vidme stle zle, lebo proste my sa dvame na obdobie rok a pol a dva roky dopredu, pred ns, ie teraz cielime vlastne na vku inflcie v roku 2004, a ak budci rok budeme vidie inflciu v roku 2005 stle naalej nad n cie, tak budeme musie v podstate pokraova. Peter Bielik: 2025. Peter Kaimr: Budeme musie pokraova so zvyovanm sadzieb alej. Peter Bielik: Pn guvernr, potom, samozrejme, nastane takto, mikropotanie, ke sa to prejav na hypotkach, ke sa to prejav na veroch. Peter Kaimr: To sa deje u dnes. Peter Bielik: To bude, to bude dobr prleitos, aby sme si to rozobrali podrobnejie. Peter Kaimr: To sa deje u dnes a na to reaguj, samozrejme, banky a vetci, ktor proste pracuj s peniazmi, Na to zareagovali klienti. Mme za sebou niekoko mesiacov obrovskho tlaku na refixcie, to znamen, banky dvali klientom monos, tak, ako minister Sulk priiel vlastne s npadom monej fixcie alebo predpokladanho vvoja cien plynu pre, pre domcnosti pri dohode na tom, ako to bude vyzera najbliie tyri roky, tak, tak podobne banky dali monos za poplatok uom vlastne fixova si rokov sadzbu. Peter Bielik: Myslel som, e ke sa, ke sa naplno prejav aj, aj to zvenie tch rokovch sadzieb, tam sa potom naplno prejav aj to prertavanie, aj ke samozrejme, sa na to u momentlne finann intitcie intenzvne pripravuj. Eurpska centrlna banka sa tm vbec netaj, tmto zmerom. Vemi pekne vm akujem, pn guvernr, za to, e ste si dnes veer nali as pre naich divkov. Peter Kaimr: akujem za pozvanie. Krsny veer ete aj vm. Peter Bielik: Prjemn veer.

Title: ECB rates must rise above neutral but QT can wait until 2023, Kazimir says (Reuters)
text: ECB rates must rise above neutral but QT can wait until 2023, Kazimir says (Reuters) 14. okt 2022 WASHINGTON, Oct 14 (Reuters) - The European Central Bank needs to raise interest rates into the so-called restrictive territory where it holds back the economy but should not start with the reduction of its balance sheet until next year, Slovak central bank chief Peter Kazimir said. Anther 75 basis point rate hike in October would be appropriate after a similar move in September and further increases may be needed, Kazimir, who sits on the ECBs rate setting Governing Council told Reuters. We wont stop at the neutral rate, we need to keep powering through," Kazimir said on the sidelines of the International Monetary Funds annual meeting in Washington. The ECB earlier said it must get to the neutral rate, where it is neither stimulating nor holding back growth but a growing number of policymakers see a need for a foray into restrictive territory to control inflation, which is now running at 10%. Beyond rate hikes, the ECB already started talking about how to run down its oversized portfolio of public and private debt, bought over the past decade in an effort to rekindle inflation. But Kazimir said an end to full reinvestments is not imminent. ..Quantitative tightening is an inevitable part of normalisation and policy tightening but it will not start this year," Kazimir said. Sources close to the discussion said that policymakers were presented with a preliminary timeline for balance sheet reduction which sees the ECB detailing these plans in December or February with actual quantitative tightening possibly starting in the second quarter of 2023. zdroj: zdroj: - can-wait-until-2023-kazimir-says-2022-10-14/

Title: Opening remarks by Governor Peter Kaimr at the Banka Slovenije listening event
text: Uvodne slovo guvernera Petra Kazimira na diskusnom podujati Banka Slovenije 10. nov 2022 The life of a central banker in Europe, England, and the U.S. is currently complicated. I would stop short of saying were in inflation hell, but theres a lot of heat out there. Klaas Knot said it nicely in D.C. a couple of weeks ago ... Monetary policy is currently more an art than science. We used to be a wallflower at the party, and now were taking away the punch bowl without even a party in sight. What can go wrong is going wrong... On top of everything. Way too many cans are being kicked down the road, everywhere in Europe end up on our doorstep in Frankfurt. Let me explain. First, our job currently is to manage a persistent decline in living standards relative to expectations. The immediate impact of the war in Ukraine on European households, businesses, and the economy is painful: rising energy and food prices coupled with increasing prospects of a recession. At the same time, the situation in Europe is markedly different compared with the of the U.S. Europe is a net importer of energy and food. So this crisis inevitably makes us poorer, at least in the short run. The problem is that the scars are going last longer: de-globalization and friendshoring, as well as the lingering global political uncertainty, make the outlook worse than expected. Right now, our post-pandemic optimism is waning. In this environment, the best we can do is to ensure that demand in the economy adjusts to this uncertainty. Theres a danger, in my view, that once the worst of the crisis is over, workers or firms will try to claw back on some of the losses suffered previously. Governments may be slow to unwind support. Fast income growth or widening profit margins could prevent inflation from coming down to our goal. We have to act preemptively in the circumstances with little reason to cheer. Second, pretty much all the risks are currently pointing toward higher inflation. I have already mentioned a few: future wage and profit pressures or de-globalization. Add the green transition to the list in the medium and longer term. There is also a lot in the current developments that we have yet to understand fully. Isabel said last week that our economic models have limits in the current situation, and I couldnt agree more. Higher energy and input prices affect firm decisions in a way that is different from past patterns. The result may well be more persistent inflation with even stronger second-round effects on wages. Current government interventions in pricing decisions could also produce future inflation swings. Last and definitely not least, we have to talk about fiscal policy. The measures adopted at present are often far from the transitory and targeted interventions we would like to see. As a result, current fiscal behavior is, in my view, rapidly becoming an inflationary risk. Future consolidation plans are not being spelled out. As a result, the forthcoming EU fiscal framework remains unclear. Third, we at the ECB are European problem solvers of last resort. The blessing and the curse of the ECB are that we can do timely and effective interventions to calm markets and restore trust in our economy. The lack of a proper fiscal union and the lack of a proper banking union brings up issues almost daily. We have been providing quick fixes for years. But, I am afraid our friends in European governments have gotten used to this. Despite all the friendly calls for action, we remain the only game in town. Offering patched-up solutions was easy for us when we supported our economy to survive the worst and fend off the risk of inflation staying way too low for far too long. One could try to justify all kinds of interventions by the price stability mandate. So lets not do that. Supporting the economy and providing favourable financing conditions when necessary is one thing, and you can count on us. But even this carries all kinds of hidden subsidies. We have now come to the end of the road. Our price stability mandate requires us to reduce our presence in the markets and reduce our support to the economy. This will come. The sooner, the better. It is absolutely vital for our credibility and the stability of the euro area that this becomes widely recognised. Overall, the next few years will be an uphill struggle for us. Accidentally, Running up the hill by Kate Bush is now back in rotation thanks to Netflixs Stranger Things, so we have an anthem for this.

Title: NBS Governor - Chart of the year: Double-digit inflation will remain in 2023, but the government will push it down significantly (e.dennikn.sk)
text: Governor N S - Graf roka: Double-digit inflation will remain in 2023, but the government will push it down significantly (e.dennikn.sk) Dec 27, 2022 Peter Kazimir  For the Governor of the National Bank of Slovakia, Peter Kazimir, the chart of the year is the return of inflation to a double-digit level.  Average price growth will slow down to 10 percent next year, thanks to capped energy prices for households. However, these will only provide relief In the short term, energy prices will rise further.  With this text, the head of the central bank opens the Dennik E series Charts of the Year, in which prominent Slovak economists take stock of the past year and estimate what will come next. The beginning of this century. That was the last time we experienced such a high price growth in Slovakia, which was troubling households, the business sector and the economy. The topic of inflation has been kept in the background for many years. The Russian invasion of Ukraine has changed everything. She turned the world upside down. Uncertainty and volatility, problems with gas supplies, all together at a rocket pace has shot up energy prices. The inflation equation here is relatively simple - high energy prices drive inflation upwards, fundamentally. First directly and then indirectly. Energy prices affect everything in the economy: housing costs, how much we buy food, books, electronics, how much coffee or a bus ticket costs. This is one of the biggest costs for households and entrepreneurs. According to the European methodology, consumer prices rose by 15.1 percent year-on-year in November, the most since June 2000, the chart of the year shows. The inflation rate exceeded the European Central Bank's two percent target in June 2021 and has been rising continuously since then. Inflation is back Annual growth in consumer prices (HICP) Double-digit inflation will stay with us next year, but the announced government measures Next year, they will help to push down noticeably. Nevertheless, inflation will bother us for some time. Next year, it should fall from this year's 12 percent to 10 percent, and then to about 9 percent in 2024. Only in 2025 will we get below 4 percent. However, question marks continue to hang over the future development of energy prices, including those regulated for households. Short-term relief next year will sooner or later have to be reflected in prices. To what extent and in what intensity, we have to wait and see.
